import Mathlib

/-!
# The symmetry dichotomy for attention architectures

`Catalog/MachineLearning/TransformerUniversality/ContinuousUniversality.lean` proves that the
subalgebra generated by linear-attention readouts is uniformly dense in the continuous
functionals of a sequence, and
`Catalog/MachineLearning/TransformerUniversality/PositionalSymmetry.lean` shows that additive
positional encodings destroy permutation symmetry.  Neither file answers the question those two
results pose together:

> *exactly which* sequence functionals can a symmetric (positional-encoding-free) attention
> architecture approximate, and does positional encoding really restore everything?

This file answers both, and does so at the natural level of generality: an arbitrary **finite
group of token symmetries**, presented as a homomorphism `act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι`.  Taking
`Γ = Equiv.Perm ι` with `act = id` recovers the fully permutation-symmetric (absolute-position
free) transformer; taking `Γ` cyclic recovers relative/shift-equivariant attention.

Write `Seq ι κ = ι → κ → ℝ` for length-`ι` sequences of `κ`-dimensional features and let
`permAct σ x = x ∘ σ` be the token-permutation action.  The architecture class is the
`ℝ`-subalgebra `attentionAlgebra` generated by the linear attention readouts (a readout with
uniform softmax weights is literally a uniform-attention head, see
`softmaxHeadRead_zero_scores`), and the *symmetric* class is its subset of `Γ`-invariant
elements.

Main results.

* `group_uniform_universal` — **positive half**: on every compact `Γ`-saturated set of
  sequences, every `Γ`-invariant continuous functional is uniformly approximated by a
  `Γ`-invariant element of `attentionAlgebra`.  The proof runs Stone–Weierstrass and then
  averages the approximant over `Γ`, which needs the algebra to be stable under the action
  (`attentionAlgebra_compPerm_mem`).  `symmetric_uniform_universal` and
  `shift_uniform_universal` are the full-symmetric and cyclic-shift specializations.
* `invariant_defect_lower_bound`, `symmetric_class_closed_under_uniform_limits`,
  `orbit_barrier_lower`, `orbit_barrier_attained` — **negative half**: the invariant class is
  uniformly closed and the optimal invariant error on an orbit is *exactly* half the orbit
  oscillation.  `symmetry_barrier_position_read` makes this concrete: no model invariant under
  a permutation that moves position `i₀` reads position `i₀` to accuracy better than `1/2`.
* `positional_restores_universality`, `positional_seq2seq_universality` — **the repair**: with
  the one-hot positional encoding `posEnc`, *fully permutation-invariant* models on the
  augmented feature space `κ ⊕ ι` approximate every continuous functional, and every continuous
  sequence-to-sequence map, uniformly on compacta.  The mechanism is an explicit invariant
  continuous decoder `decodeSeq` inverting `posEnc`.
* `equivariant_uniform_universal` — **exact converse**: through the marked-token encoding,
  `Γ`-invariant attention models uniformly approximate every continuous `Γ`-equivariant
  sequence-to-sequence map, and the resulting head family is itself exactly equivariant.  So
  the expressive power of symmetric attention is *precisely* the equivariant continuous maps.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace PermutationDichotomy

/-- Length-`ι` sequences of `κ`-dimensional real feature vectors. -/
abbrev Seq (ι κ : Type*) := ι → κ → ℝ

section Action

variable {ι κ : Type*}

/-- The token-permutation action on sequences: `permAct σ x` reads position `i` of the
permuted sequence off position `σ i` of the original. -/
def permAct (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) (x : Seq ι κ) : Seq ι κ := fun i => x (σ i)

@[simp] theorem permAct_one (x : Seq ι κ) : permAct (1 : Equiv.Perm ι) x = x := rfl

theorem permAct_comp (σ τ : Equiv.Perm ι) (x : Seq ι κ) :
    permAct σ (permAct τ x) = permAct (τ * σ) x := rfl

theorem continuous_permAct (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) : Continuous (permAct σ (κ := κ)) :=
  continuous_pi fun i => continuous_apply (σ i)

/-- The permutation action as a continuous map. -/
def permCM (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) : C(Seq ι κ, Seq ι κ) := ⟨permAct σ, continuous_permAct σ⟩

@[simp] theorem permCM_apply (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) (x : Seq ι κ) : permCM σ x = permAct σ x := rfl

variable {Γ : Type*} [Group Γ]

/-- A functional of a sequence is *`Γ`-invariant* when the token symmetries in `Γ` do not
change its value. -/
def InvariantUnder (act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι) (f : Seq ι κ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Γ) (x : Seq ι κ), f (permAct (act g) x) = f x

/-- A set of sequences is *`Γ`-saturated* when it is closed under the token symmetries. -/
def SaturatedUnder (act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι) (K : Set (Seq ι κ)) : Prop :=
  ∀ g : Γ, ∀ x ∈ K, permAct (act g) x ∈ K

/-- Invariance under the *full* symmetric group of the token positions. -/
abbrev Invariant (f : Seq ι κ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  InvariantUnder (MonoidHom.id (Equiv.Perm ι)) f

/-- Saturation under the *full* symmetric group of the token positions. -/
abbrev Saturated (K : Set (Seq ι κ)) : Prop :=
  SaturatedUnder (MonoidHom.id (Equiv.Perm ι)) K

end Action

section Architecture

variable {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ]

/-- A linear attention readout with fixed weights, as a continuous functional. -/
noncomputable def readoutCM (w : Seq ι κ) : C(Seq ι κ, ℝ) where
  toFun x := ∑ i, ∑ a, w i a * x i a
  continuous_toFun := by
    apply continuous_finset_sum
    intro i _
    apply continuous_finset_sum
    intro a _
    exact continuous_const.mul ((continuous_apply a).comp (continuous_apply i))

@[simp] theorem readoutCM_apply (w x : Seq ι κ) : readoutCM w x = ∑ i, ∑ a, w i a * x i a := rfl

/-- A genuine softmax attention read: value `∑ a, w j a * x j a` at token `j`, weighted by the
softmax of the scores `s`. -/
noncomputable def softmaxHeadRead (s : ι → ℝ) (w : Seq ι κ) (x : Seq ι κ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ j, (Real.exp (s j) / ∑ k, Real.exp (s k)) * (∑ a, w j a * x j a)

/-- **The readouts are honest attention heads.**  A softmax head with vanishing scores (uniform
attention) is exactly a linear readout with rescaled weights. -/
theorem softmaxHeadRead_zero_scores (w x : Seq ι κ) :
    softmaxHeadRead (fun _ => 0) w x
      = readoutCM (fun j a => w j a / (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)) x := by
  simp only [softmaxHeadRead, readoutCM_apply, Real.exp_zero, Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul,
    mul_one, Finset.card_univ]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
  intro j _
  rw [Finset.mul_sum]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
  intro a _
  field_simp

/-- The architecture class: the `ℝ`-subalgebra of continuous functionals generated by the
linear attention readouts (attention heads followed by multiplicative mixing). -/
noncomputable def attentionAlgebra (ι κ : Type*) [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] :
    Subalgebra ℝ C(Seq ι κ, ℝ) :=
  Algebra.adjoin ℝ (Set.range (readoutCM (ι := ι) (κ := κ)))

theorem readout_mem_attentionAlgebra (w : Seq ι κ) : readoutCM w ∈ attentionAlgebra ι κ :=
  Algebra.subset_adjoin ⟨w, rfl⟩

/-- One-hot weights turn a readout into a coordinate evaluation. -/
theorem readoutCM_oneHot [DecidableEq ι] [DecidableEq κ] (i₀ : ι) (a₀ : κ) (x : Seq ι κ) :
    readoutCM (fun i a => if i = i₀ ∧ a = a₀ then (1:ℝ) else 0) x = x i₀ a₀ := by
  show ∑ i, ∑ a, (if i = i₀ ∧ a = a₀ then (1:ℝ) else 0) * x i a = x i₀ a₀
  rw [Finset.sum_eq_single i₀]
  · rw [Finset.sum_eq_single a₀]
    · simp
    · intro a _ ha; simp [ha]
    · intro h; exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ a₀) h
  · intro i _ hi
    apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
    intro a _
    simp [hi]
  · intro h; exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ i₀) h

/-- Readouts separate sequences, so the architecture class does. -/
theorem attentionAlgebra_separatesPoints : (attentionAlgebra ι κ).SeparatesPoints := by
  classical
  intro x y hxy
  obtain ⟨i₀, hi⟩ : ∃ i, x i ≠ y i := by
    by_contra h
    push_neg at h
    exact hxy (funext h)
  obtain ⟨a₀, ha⟩ : ∃ a, x i₀ a ≠ y i₀ a := by
    by_contra h
    push_neg at h
    exact

functionals of a sequence, and
`Catalog/MachineLearning/TransformerUniversality/PositionalSymmetry.lean` shows that additive
positional encodings destroy permutation symmetry.  Neither file answers the question those two
results pose together:

> *exactly which* sequence functionals can a symmetric (positional-encoding-free) attention
> architecture approximate, and does positional encoding really restore everything?

This file answers both, and does so at the natural level of generality: an arbitrary **finite
group of token symmetries**, presented as a homomorphism `act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι`.  Taking
`Γ = Equiv.Perm ι` with `act = id` recovers the fully permutation-symmetric (absolute-position
free) transformer; taking `Γ` cyclic recovers relative/shift-equivariant attention.

Write `Seq ι κ = ι → κ → ℝ` for length-`ι` sequences of `κ`-dimensional features and let
`permAct σ x = x ∘ σ` be the token-permutation action.  The architecture class is the
`ℝ`-subalgebra `attentionAlgebra` generated by the linear attention readouts (a readout with
uniform softmax weights is literally a uniform-attention head, see
`softmaxHeadRead_zero_scores`), and the *symmetric* class is its subset of `Γ`-invariant
elements.

Main results.

* `group_uniform_universal` — **positive half**: on every compact `Γ`-saturated set of
  sequences, every `Γ`-invariant continuous functional is uniformly approximated by a
  `Γ`-invariant element of `attentionAlgebra`.  The proof runs Stone–Weierstrass and then
  averages the approximant over `Γ`, which needs the algebra to be stable under the action
  (`attentionAlgebra_compPerm_mem`).  `symmetric_uniform_universal` and
  `shift_uniform_universal` are the full-symmetric and cyclic-shift specializations.
* `invariant_defect_lower_bound`, `symmetric_class_closed_under_uniform_limits`,
  `orbit_barrier_lower`, `orbit_barrier_attained` — **negative half**: the invariant class is
  uniformly closed and the optimal invariant error on an orbit is *exactly* half the orbit
  oscillation.  `symmetry_barrier_position_read` makes this concrete: no model invariant under
  a permutation that moves position `i₀` reads position `i₀` to accuracy better than `1/2`.
* `positional_restores_universality`, `positional_seq2seq_universality` — **the repair**: with
  the one-hot positional encoding `posEnc`, *fully permutation-invariant* models on the
  augmented feature space `κ ⊕ ι` approximate every continuous functional, and every continuous
  sequence-to-sequence map, uniformly on compacta.  The mechanism is an explicit invariant
  continuous decoder `decodeSeq` inverting `posEnc`.
* `equivariant_uniform_universal` — **exact converse**: through the marked-token encoding,
  `Γ`-invariant attention models uniformly approximate every continuous `Γ`-equivariant
  sequence-to-sequence map, and the resulting head family is itself exactly equivariant.  So
  the expressive power of symmetric attention is *precisely* the equivariant continuous maps.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace PermutationDichotomy

/-- Length-`ι` sequences of `κ`-dimensional real feature vectors. -/
abbrev Seq (ι κ : Type*) := ι → κ → ℝ

section Action

variable {ι κ : Type*}

/-- The token-permutation action on sequences: `permAct σ x` reads position `i` of the
permuted sequence off position `σ i` of the original. -/
def permAct (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) (x : Seq ι κ) : Seq ι κ := fun i => x (σ i)

@[simp] theorem permAct_one (x : Seq ι κ) : permAct (1 : Equiv.Perm ι) x = x := rfl

theorem permAct_comp (σ τ : Equiv.Perm ι) (x : Seq ι κ) :
    permAct σ (permAct τ x) = permAct (τ * σ) x := rfl

theorem continuous_permAct (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) : Continuous (permAct σ (κ := κ)) :=
  continuous_pi fun i => continuous_apply (σ i)

/-- The permutation action as a continuous map. -/
def permCM (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) : C(Seq ι κ, Seq ι κ) := ⟨permAct σ, continuous_permAct σ⟩

@[simp] theorem permCM_apply (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) (x : Seq ι κ) : permCM σ x = permAct σ x := rfl

variable {Γ : Type*} [Group Γ]

/-- A functional of a sequence is *`Γ`-invariant* when the token symmetries in `Γ` do not
change its value. -/
def InvariantUnder (act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι) (f : Seq ι κ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Γ) (x : Seq ι κ), f (permAct (act g) x) = f x

/-- A set of sequences is *`Γ`-saturated* when it is closed under the token symmetries. -/
def SaturatedUnder (act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι) (K : Set (Seq ι κ)) : Prop :=
  ∀ g : Γ, ∀ x ∈ K, permAct (act g) x ∈ K

/-- Invariance under the *full* symmetric group of the token positions. -/
abbrev Invariant (f : Seq ι κ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  InvariantUnder (MonoidHom.id (Equiv.Perm ι)) f

/-- Saturation under the *full* symmetric group of the token positions. -/
abbrev Saturated (K : Set (Seq ι κ)) : Prop :=
  SaturatedUnder (MonoidHom.id (Equiv.Perm ι)) K

end Action

section Architecture

variable {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ]

/-- A linear attention readout with fixed weights, as a continuous functional. -/
noncomputable def readoutCM (w : Seq ι κ) : C(Seq ι κ, ℝ) where
  toFun x := ∑ i, ∑ a, w i a * x i a
  continuous_toFun := by
    apply continuous_finset_sum
    intro i _
    apply continuous_finset_sum
    intro a _
    exact continuous_const.mul ((continuous_apply a).comp (continuous_apply i))

@[simp] theorem readoutCM_apply (w x : Seq ι κ) : readoutCM w x = ∑ i, ∑ a, w i a * x i a := rfl

/-- A genuine softmax attention read: value `∑ a, w j a * x j a` at token `j`, weighted by the
softmax of the scores `s`. -/
noncomputable def softmaxHeadRead (s : ι → ℝ) (w : Seq ι κ) (x : Seq ι κ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ j, (Real.exp (s j) / ∑ k, Real.exp (s k)) * (∑ a, w j a * x j a)

/-- **The readouts are honest attention heads.**  A softmax head with vanishing scores (uniform
attention) is exactly a linear readout with rescaled weights. -/
theorem softmaxHeadRead_zero_scores (w x : Seq ι κ) :
    softmaxHeadRead (fun _ => 0) w x
      = readoutCM (fun j a => w j a / (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)) x := by
  simp only [softmaxHeadRead, readoutCM_apply, Real.exp_zero, Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul,
    mul_one, Finset.card_univ]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
  intro j _
  rw [Finset.mul_sum]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
  intro a _
  field_simp

/-- The architecture class: the `ℝ`-subalgebra of continuous functionals generated by the
linear attention readouts (attention heads followed by multiplicative mixing). -/
noncomputable def attentionAlgebra (ι κ : Type*) [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] :
    Subalgebra ℝ C(Seq ι κ, ℝ) :=
  Algebra.adjoin ℝ (Set.range (readoutCM (ι := ι) (κ := κ)))

theorem readout_mem_attentionAlgebra (w : Seq ι κ) : readoutCM w ∈ attentionAlgebra ι κ :=
  Algebra.subset_adjoin ⟨w, rfl⟩

/-- One-hot weights turn a readout into a coordinate evaluation. -/
theorem readoutCM_oneHot [DecidableEq ι] [DecidableEq κ] (i₀ : ι) (a₀ : κ) (x : Seq ι κ) :
    readoutCM (fun i a => if i = i₀ ∧ a = a₀ then (1:ℝ) else 0) x = x i₀ a₀ := by
  show ∑ i, ∑ a, (if i = i₀ ∧ a = a₀ then (1:ℝ) else 0) * x i a = x i₀ a₀
  rw [Finset.sum_eq_single i₀]
  · rw [Finset.sum_eq_single a₀]
    · simp
    · intro a _ ha; simp [ha]
    · intro h; exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ a₀) h
  · intro i _ hi
    apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
    intro a _
    simp [hi]
  · intro h; exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ i₀) h

/-- Readouts separate sequences, so the architecture class does. -/
theorem attentionAlgebra_separatesPoints : (attentionAlgebra ι κ).SeparatesPoints := by
  classical
  intro x y hxy
  obtain ⟨i₀, hi⟩ : ∃ i, x i ≠ y i := by
    by_contra h
    push_neg at h
    exact hxy (funext h)
  obtain ⟨a₀, ha⟩ : ∃ a, x i₀ a ≠ y i₀ a := by
    by_contra h
    push_neg at h
    exact hi (funext h)
  refine ⟨readoutCM (fun i a => if i = i₀ ∧ a = a₀ then (1:ℝ) else 0), ?_, ?_⟩
  · exact ⟨readoutCM (fun i a => if i = i₀ ∧ a = a₀ then (1:ℝ) else 0),
      Algebra.subset_adjoin ⟨_, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
  · rw [readoutCM_oneHot, readoutCM_oneHot]
    exact ha

end Architecture

section GroupStability

variable {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ]

/-- Precomposition of a readout with a token permutation is again a readout. -/
theorem readoutCM_comp_permCM (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) (w : Seq ι κ) :
    (ContinuousMap.compRightAlgHom ℝ ℝ (permCM σ)) (readoutCM w)
      = readoutCM (fun i a => w (σ.symm i) a) := by
  ext x
  show ∑ i, ∑ a, w i a * x (σ i) a = ∑ i, ∑ a, w (σ.symm i) a * x i a
  rw [← Equiv.sum_comp σ (fun j => ∑ a, w (σ.symm j) a * x j a)]
  simp

/-- **The architecture class is stable under the token-permutation action.** -/
theorem attentionAlgebra_compPerm_mem (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) {p : C(Seq ι κ, ℝ)}
    (hp : p ∈ attentionAlgebra ι κ) :
    (ContinuousMap.compRightAlgHom ℝ ℝ (permCM σ)) p ∈ attentionAlgebra ι κ := by
  have hsub :
      attentionAlgebra ι κ ≤
        (attentionAlgebra ι κ).comap (ContinuousMap.compRightAlgHom ℝ ℝ (permCM σ)) := by
    apply Algebra.adjoin_le
    rintro _ ⟨w, rfl⟩
    show (ContinuousMap.compRightAlgHom ℝ ℝ (permCM σ)) (readoutCM w) ∈ attentionAlgebra ι κ
    rw [readoutCM_comp_permCM]
    exact readout_mem_attentionAlgebra _
  exact hsub hp

end GroupStability

section Symmetrization

variable {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] {Γ : Type*} [Group Γ] [Fintype Γ]

/-- Group averaging of a model over the symmetry group `Γ`. -/
noncomputable def symmetrize (act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι) (q : C(Seq ι κ, ℝ)) : C(Seq ι κ, ℝ) :=
  (Fintype.card Γ : ℝ)⁻¹ •
    ∑ g : Γ, (ContinuousMap.compRightAlgHom ℝ ℝ (permCM (act g))) q

omit [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] in
theorem symmetrize_apply (act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι) (q : C(Seq ι κ, ℝ)) (x : Seq ι κ) :
    symmetrize act q x = (Fintype.card Γ : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ g : Γ, q (permAct (act g) x) := by
  simp [symmetrize]

/-- Averaging keeps a model inside the architecture class. -/
theorem symmetrize_mem (act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι) {q : C(Seq ι κ, ℝ)}
    (hq : q ∈ attentionAlgebra ι κ) :
    symmetrize act q ∈ attentionAlgebra ι κ :=
  Subalgebra.smul_mem _
    (Subalgebra.sum_mem _ fun g _ => attentionAlgebra_compPerm_mem (act g) hq) _

omit [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] in
/-- **Averaging produces an invariant model.** -/
theorem symmetrize_invariant (act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι) (q : C(Seq ι κ, ℝ)) :
    InvariantUnder act (fun x => symmetrize act q x) := by
  intro tau x
  simp only [symmetrize_apply]
  congr 1
  rw [← Equiv.sum_comp (Equiv.mulLeft tau) (fun rho : Γ => q (permAct (act rho) x))]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
  intro g _
  rw [permAct_comp, ← MonoidHom.map_mul]
  rfl

omit [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] in
/-- Averaging does not degrade the approximation quality of an invariant target on a
saturated set. -/
theorem symmetrize_error (act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι) {q : C(Seq ι κ, ℝ)} {g : Seq ι κ → ℝ}
    (hg : InvariantUnder act g) {K : Set (Seq ι κ)} (hKsat : SaturatedUnder act K) {eps : ℝ}
    (hq : ∀ x ∈ K, |q x - g x| < eps) :
    ∀ x ∈ K, |symmetrize act q x - g x| < eps := by
  intro x hx
  haveI : Nonempty Γ := ⟨1⟩
  have hcardR : (0:ℝ) < (Fintype.card Γ : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast Fintype.card_pos (α := Γ)
  have hsum : ∀ gamma : Γ, |q (permAct (act gamma) x) - g x| < eps := by
    intro gamma
    have := hq (permAct (act gamma) x) (hKsat gamma x hx)
    rwa [hg gamma x] at this
  have hkey : |∑ gamma : Γ, (q (permAct (act gamma) x) - g x)| < (Fintype.card Γ : ℝ) * eps := by
    calc |∑ gamma : Γ, (q (permAct (act gamma) x) - g x)|
        ≤ ∑ gamma : Γ, |q (permAct (act gamma) x) - g x| := Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
      _ < ∑ _gamma : Γ, eps := by
          refine Finset.sum_lt_sum_of_nonempty ?_ (fun gamma _ => hsum gamma)
          exact Finset.univ_nonempty
      _ = (Fintype.card Γ : ℝ) * eps := by
          simp [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, mul_comm]
  have hsplit : ∑ gamma : Γ, (q (permAct (act gamma) x) - g x)
      = (∑ gamma : Γ, q (permAct (act gamma) x)) - (Fintype.card Γ : ℝ) * g x := by
    rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul]
  have hrewrite : symmetrize act q x - g x
      = (Fintype.card Γ : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ gamma : Γ, (q (permAct (act gamma) x) - g x) := by
    rw [symmetrize_apply, hsplit, mul_sub, inv_mul_cancel_left₀ (ne_of_gt hcardR)]
  rw [hrewrite, abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg (le_of_lt (inv_pos.mpr hcardR))]
  rw [inv_mul_lt_iff₀ hcardR]
  simpa [mul_comm] using hkey

end Symmetrization

section PositiveHalf

variable {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] {Γ : Type*} [Group Γ] [Fintype Γ]

/-- **Symmetric universality for an arbitrary finite token-symmetry group.**  On every compact
`Γ`-saturated set of sequences, every `Γ`-invariant continuous functional is uniformly
approximated by a `Γ`-invariant element of the attention algebra.  This is the exact reach of
an architecture whose only structure is `Γ`-symmetry:
`symmetric_class_closed_under_uniform_limits` shows nothing outside the invariant class is
reachable. -/
theorem group_uniform_universal (act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι) (g : C(Seq ι κ, ℝ))
    (hg : InvariantUnder act (fun x => g x)) {K : Set (Seq ι κ)} (hK : IsCompact K)
    (hKsat : SaturatedUnder act K) {eps : ℝ} (heps : 0 < eps) :
    ∃ p ∈ attentionAlgebra ι κ,
      InvariantUnder act (fun x => p x) ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, |p x - g x| < eps := by
  obtain ⟨q, hq, hclose⟩ :=
    ContinuousMap.exists_mem_subalgebra_near_continuous_of_isCompact_of_separatesPoints
      (A := attentionAlgebra ι κ) attentionAlgebra_separatesPoints g hK heps
  refine ⟨symmetrize act q, symmetrize_mem act hq, symmetrize_invariant act q, ?_⟩
  refine symmetrize_error act hg hKsat ?_
  intro x hx
  simpa [Real.norm_eq_abs] using hclose x hx

variable [DecidableEq ι]

/-- **Full permutation symmetry.**  Specialization of `group_uniform_universal` to the whole
symmetric group: a positional-encoding-free attention architecture uniformly approximates
exactly the permutation-invariant continuous functionals. -/
theorem symmetric_uniform_universal (g : C(Seq ι κ, ℝ)) (hg : Invariant (fun x => g x))
    {K : Set (Seq ι κ)} (hK : IsCompact K) (hKsat : Saturated K) {eps : ℝ} (heps : 0 < eps) :
    ∃ p ∈ attentionAlgebra ι κ,
      Invariant (fun x => p x) ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, |p x - g x| < eps :=
  group_uniform_universal (MonoidHom.id (Equiv.Perm ι)) g hg hK hKsat heps

omit [DecidableEq ι] in
/-- **Relative (cyclic) symmetry.**  Specialization to the group generated by a single
permutation `r` — the shift group modelled by relative positional encodings.  Every
shift-invariant continuous functional is uniformly approximated by a shift-invariant attention
model. -/
theorem shift_uniform_universal (r : Equiv.Perm ι) (g : C(Seq ι κ, ℝ))
    (hg : ∀ (k : ℕ) (x : Seq ι κ), g (permAct (r ^ k) x) = g x)
    {K : Set (Seq ι κ)} (hK : IsCompact K)
    (hKsat : ∀ k : ℕ, ∀ x ∈ K, permAct (r ^ k) x ∈ K) {eps : ℝ} (heps : 0 < eps) :
    ∃ p ∈ attentionAlgebra ι κ,
      (∀ (k : ℕ) (x : Seq ι κ), p (permAct (r ^ k) x) = p x) ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, |p x - g x| < eps := by
  classical
  haveI : Fintype (Subgroup.zpowers r) := Fintype.ofFinite _
  have hpow : ∀ s : Subgroup.zpowers r, ∃ k : ℕ, r ^ k = (s : Equiv.Perm ι) := by
    intro s
    have hs : (s : Equiv.Perm ι) ∈ Subgroup.zpowers r := s.2
    rw [← mem_powers_iff_mem_zpowers] at hs
    obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hs
    exact ⟨k, hk⟩
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpinv, hclose⟩ :=
    group_uniform_universal (Γ := Subgroup.zpowers r) (Subgroup.zpowers r).subtype g
      (by
        intro s x
        obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hpow s
        show g (permAct (s : Equiv.Perm ι) x) = g x
        rw [← hk]
        exact hg k x)
      hK
      (by
        intro s x hx
        obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hpow s
        show permAct (s : Equiv.Perm ι) x ∈ K
        rw [← hk]
        exact hKsat k x hx)
      heps
  refine ⟨p, hp, ?_, hclose⟩
  intro k x
  exact hpinv ⟨r ^ k, Subgroup.mem_zpowers_iff.mpr ⟨(k : ℤ), by simp⟩⟩ x

end PositiveHalf

section NegativeHalf

variable {ι κ : Type*}

/-- **The invariance defect is an approximation barrier.**  Any model invariant under a single
token permutation `σ` pays, somewhere on the `σ`-orbit, at least half of the target's defect
along `σ`. -/
theorem invariant_defect_lower_bound {p g : Seq ι κ → ℝ} {σ : Equiv.Perm ι}
    (hp : ∀ x, p (permAct σ x) = p x) (x : Seq ι κ) :
    |g x - g (permAct σ x)| ≤ |p x - g x| + |p (permAct σ x) - g (permAct σ x)| := by
  have h : g x - g (permAct σ x)
      = -(p x - g x) + (p (permAct σ x) - g (permAct σ x)) := by
    rw [hp x]; ring
  calc |g x - g (permAct σ x)|
      ≤ |-(p x - g x)| + |p (permAct σ x) - g (permAct σ x)| := by
        rw [h]; exact abs_add_le _ _
    _ = |p x - g x| + |p (permAct σ x) - g (permAct σ x)| := by rw [abs_neg]

/-- **The symmetric class is uniformly closed.**  A functional approximated to arbitrary
accuracy by `σ`-invariant models on a `σ`-stable set is itself `σ`-invariant there. -/
theorem symmetric_class_closed_under_uniform_limits {g : Seq ι κ → ℝ} {K : Set (Seq ι κ)}
    {σ : Equiv.Perm ι} (hKsat : ∀ x ∈ K, permAct σ x ∈ K)
    (h : ∀ eps > 0, ∃ p : Seq ι κ → ℝ,
      (∀ y, p (permAct σ y) = p y) ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, |p x - g x| < eps)
    (x : Seq ι κ) (hx : x ∈ K) :
    g (permAct σ x) = g x := by
  have hzero : g x - g (permAct σ x) = 0 := by
    by_contra hne
    have hd : 0 < |g x - g (permAct σ x)| := abs_pos.mpr hne
    obtain ⟨p, hp, hclose⟩ := h (|g x - g (permAct σ x)| / 4) (by linarith)
    have h1 := hclose x hx
    have h2 := hclose (permAct σ x) (hKsat x hx)
    have h3 := invariant_defect_lower_bound (g := g) hp x
    linarith
  linarith

/-- **The symmetry barrier is exactly half the orbit oscillation (lower bound).**  On the orbit
of a single sequence, no invariant model beats half the spread of the target. -/
theorem orbit_barrier_lower [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (g : Seq ι κ → ℝ) (x : Seq ι κ)
    {p : Seq ι κ → ℝ} (hp : Invariant p) :
    ((Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty fun σ : Equiv.Perm ι => g (permAct σ x))
        - Finset.univ.inf' Finset.univ_nonempty fun σ : Equiv.Perm ι => g (permAct σ x)) / 2
      ≤ Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty
          fun σ : Equiv.Perm ι => |p (permAct σ x) - g (permAct σ x)| := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨sM, -, hsM⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_sup' (Finset.univ_nonempty (α := Equiv.Perm ι))
    (fun σ : Equiv.Perm ι => g (permAct σ x))
  obtain ⟨sm, -, hsm⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_inf' (Finset.univ_nonempty (α := Equiv.Perm ι))
    (fun σ : Equiv.Perm ι => g (permAct σ x))
  have hM : |p (permAct sM x) - g (permAct sM x)|
      ≤ Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty
          fun σ : Equiv.Perm ι => |p (permAct σ x) - g (permAct σ x)| :=
    Finset.le_sup' (fun σ : Equiv.Perm ι => |p (permAct σ x) - g (permAct σ x)|)
      (Finset.mem_univ sM)
  have hm : |p (permAct sm x) - g (permAct sm x)|
      ≤ Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty
          fun σ : Equiv.Perm ι => |p (permAct σ x) - g (permAct σ x)| :=
    Finset.le_sup' (fun σ : Equiv.Perm ι => |p (permAct σ x) - g (permAct σ x)|)
      (Finset.mem_univ sm)
  have e1 : p (permAct sM x) = p x := hp sM x
  have e2 : p (permAct sm x) = p x := hp sm x
  have hconst : p (permAct sM x) = p (permAct sm x) := by rw [e1, e2]
  have h1 : g (permAct sM x) - p (permAct sM x) ≤ |p (permAct sM x) - g (permAct sM x)| := by
    rw [abs_sub_comm]; exact le_abs_self _
  have h2 : p (permAct sm x) - g (permAct sm x) ≤ |p (permAct sm x) - g (permAct sm x)| :=
    le_abs_self _
  rw [hsM, hsm]
  linarith

/-- **The bound is attained**: the constant midpoint model is invariant and achieves exactly
half the orbit oscillation, so `orbit_barrier_lower` is sharp. -/
theorem orbit_barrier_attained [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (g : Seq ι κ → ℝ) (x : Seq ι κ) :
    ∃ p : Seq ι κ → ℝ, Invariant p ∧ ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm ι,
      |p (permAct σ x) - g (permAct σ x)|
        ≤ ((Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty fun τ : Equiv.Perm ι => g (permAct τ x))
            - Finset.univ.inf' Finset.univ_nonempty
                fun τ : Equiv.Perm ι => g (permAct τ x)) / 2 := by
  classical
  set M := Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty fun τ : Equiv.Perm ι => g (permAct τ x) with hMdef
  set m := Finset.univ.inf' Finset.univ_nonempty fun τ : Equiv.Perm ι => g (permAct τ x) with hmdef
  refine ⟨fun _ => (M + m) / 2, fun _ _ => rfl, ?_⟩
  intro σ
  have hle : g (permAct σ x) ≤ M := by
    rw [hMdef]
    exact Finset.le_sup' (fun τ : Equiv.Perm ι => g (permAct τ x)) (Finset.mem_univ σ)
  have hge : m ≤ g (permAct σ x) := by
    rw [hmdef]
    exact Finset.inf'_le (fun τ : Equiv.Perm ι => g (permAct τ x)) (Finset.mem_univ σ)
  rw [abs_le]
  constructor <;> linarith

/-- **The symmetry barrier for position reading.**  If a token symmetry `σ` moves position `i₀`,
then no `σ`-invariant model reads position `i₀` to uniform accuracy better than `1/2`.  This
applies verbatim to fully permutation-symmetric models and to shift-symmetric (relative
positional encoding) models. -/
theorem symmetry_barrier_position_read [DecidableEq ι] [DecidableEq κ] {σ : Equiv.Perm ι}
    {i₀ : ι} (hne : σ i₀ ≠ i₀) (a₀ : κ) (p : Seq ι κ → ℝ)
    (hp : ∀ x, p (permAct σ x) = p x) :
    ∃ x : Seq ι κ, (1:ℝ)/2 ≤ |p x - x i₀ a₀| := by
  classical
  set u : Seq ι κ := fun i a => if i = i₀ ∧ a = a₀ then (1:ℝ) else 0 with hu
  have hu0 : u i₀ a₀ = 1 := by simp [hu]
  have hv0 : (permAct σ u) i₀ a₀ = 0 := by
    show u (σ i₀) a₀ = 0
    simp [hu, hne]
  have hdefect := invariant_defect_lower_bound (g := fun y : Seq ι κ => y i₀ a₀) hp u
  simp only [hu0, hv0] at hdefect
  by_cases h : (1:ℝ)/2 ≤ |p u - u i₀ a₀|
  · exact ⟨u, h⟩
  · refine ⟨permAct σ u, ?_⟩
    push_neg at h
    rw [hu0] at h
    rw [hv0]
    have habs : |(1:ℝ) - 0| = 1 := by norm_num
    rw [habs] at hdefect
    linarith

/-- **A concrete symmetry barrier.**  Reading the first token of a two-token sequence is beyond
every permutation-invariant model: the uniform error is at least `1/2`.  Smallest instance of
`symmetry_barrier_position_read`. -/
theorem no_symmetric_model_reads_first_token
    (p : Seq (Fin 2) (Fin 1) → ℝ) (hp : Invariant p) :
    ∃ x : Seq (Fin 2) (Fin 1), (1:ℝ)/2 ≤ |p x - x 0 0| :=
  symmetry_barrier_position_read (σ := Equiv.swap 0 1) (i₀ := 0) (by decide) 0 p
    (fun x => hp (Equiv.swap 0 1) x)

end NegativeHalf

section PositionalRepair

variable {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ]

/-- One-hot positional encoding: each token keeps its features and acquires an extra block of
`ι` coordinates holding the indicator of its own position. -/
def posEnc (x : Seq ι κ) : Seq ι (κ ⊕ ι) :=
  fun i => Sum.elim (x i) (fun j => if j = i then (1:ℝ) else 0)

omit [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] in
theorem continuous_posEnc : Continuous (posEnc (ι := ι) (κ := κ)) := by
  apply continuous_pi
  intro i
  apply continuous_pi
  intro c
  cases c with
  | inl a => exact (continuous_apply a).comp (continuous_apply i)
  | inr j => exact continuous_const

/-- Positionally tagged sequences can be decoded *invariantly*: attending from the tag block to
the feature block reconstructs the ordered sequence, and the reconstruction is a sum over
tokens, hence permutation invariant. -/
def decodeSeq (z : Seq ι (κ ⊕ ι)) : Seq ι κ :=
  fun i a => ∑ j, z j (Sum.inr i) * z j (Sum.inl a)

omit [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ] in
theorem continuous_decodeSeq : Continuous (decodeSeq (ι := ι) (κ := κ)) := by
  apply continuous_pi
  intro i
  apply continuous_pi
  intro a
  apply continuous_finset_sum
  intro j _
  have h1 : Continuous fun z : Seq ι (κ ⊕ ι) => z j (Sum.inr i) :=
    (continuous_apply (Sum.inr i)).comp (continuous_apply j)
  have h2 : Continuous fun z : Seq ι (κ ⊕ ι) => z j (Sum.inl a) :=
    (continuous_apply (Sum.inl a)).comp (continuous_apply j)
  exact h1.mul h2

omit [Fintype κ] in
/-- **The decoder inverts the positional encoding.** -/
theorem decodeSeq_posEnc (x : Seq ι κ) : decodeSeq (posEnc x) = x := by
  funext i a
  show ∑ j, (if i = j then (1:ℝ) else 0) * x j a = x i a
  rw [Finset.sum_eq_single i]
  · simp
  · intro j _ hj
    simp [Ne.symm hj]
  · intro h; exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ i) h

omit [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ] in
/-- **The decoder is permutation invariant**, so any functional built through it is invariant. -/
theorem decodeSeq_invariant (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) (z : Seq ι (κ ⊕ ι)) :
    decodeSeq (permAct σ z) = decodeSeq z := by
  funext i a
  show ∑ j, z (σ j) (Sum.inr i) * z (σ j) (Sum.inl a)
      = ∑ j, z j (Sum.inr i) * z j (Sum.inl a)
  exact Equiv.sum_comp σ (fun j => z j (Sum.inr i) * z j (Sum.inl a))

/-- The saturation of the positionally encoded image of a set. -/
def encSaturation (K : Set (Seq ι κ)) : Set (Seq ι (κ ⊕ ι)) :=
  ⋃ σ : Equiv.Perm ι, (permAct σ) '' (posEnc '' K)

omit [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] in
theorem posEnc_mem_encSaturation {K : Set (Seq ι κ)} {x : Seq ι κ} (hx : x ∈ K) :
    posEnc x ∈ encSaturation K :=
  Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨1, ⟨posEnc x, ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩, rfl⟩⟩

omit [Fintype κ] in
theorem isCompact_encSaturation {K : Set (Seq ι κ)} (hK : IsCompact K) :
    IsCompact (encSaturation K) :=
  isCompact_iUnion fun σ =>
    ((hK.image continuous_posEnc).image (continuous_permAct σ))

omit [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] in
theorem saturated_encSaturation (K : Set (Seq ι κ)) : Saturated (encSaturation K) := by
  rintro tau z hz
  rw [encSaturation, Set.mem_iUnion] at hz ⊢
  obtain ⟨σ, w, hw, rfl⟩ := hz
  exact ⟨σ * tau, w, hw, (permAct_comp tau σ w).symm ▸ rfl⟩

/-- **Positional encodings restore full universality.**  With the one-hot positional encoding,
*permutation-invariant* models on the augmented feature space `κ ⊕ ι` approximate every
continuous sequence functional uniformly on every compact set — including all the
order-sensitive functionals ruled out by `symmetry_barrier_position_read`. -/
theorem positional_restores_universality (g : C(Seq ι κ, ℝ)) {K : Set (Seq ι κ)}
    (hK : IsCompact K) {eps : ℝ} (heps : 0 < eps) :
    ∃ p ∈ attentionAlgebra ι (κ ⊕ ι),
      Invariant (fun z => p z) ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, |p (posEnc x) - g x| < eps := by
  set G : C(Seq ι (κ ⊕ ι), ℝ) := g.comp ⟨decodeSeq, continuous_decodeSeq⟩ with hG
  have hGinv : Invariant (fun z => G z) := by
    intro σ z
    show g (decodeSeq (permAct σ z)) = g (decodeSeq z)
    rw [decodeSeq_invariant]
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpinv, hclose⟩ :=
    symmetric_uniform_universal (ι := ι) (κ := κ ⊕ ι) G hGinv
      (isCompact_encSaturation hK) (saturated_encSaturation K) heps
  refine ⟨p, hp, hpinv, ?_⟩
  intro x hx
  have := hclose (posEnc x) (posEnc_mem_encSaturation hx)
  have hGx : G (posEnc x) = g x := by
    show g (decodeSeq (posEnc x)) = g x
    rw [decodeSeq_posEnc]
  rwa [hGx] at this

/-- **Sequence-to-sequence universality with positional encoding.**  Every continuous map from
sequences to sequences is approximated, uniformly on compacta and simultaneously in all output
positions and features, by permutation-invariant attention models applied to the positionally
encoded input. -/
theorem positional_seq2seq_universality (F : Seq ι κ → Seq ι κ)
    (hF : ∀ i a, Continuous fun x => F x i a) {K : Set (Seq ι κ)} (hK : IsCompact K)
    {eps : ℝ} (heps : 0 < eps) :
    ∃ P : ι → κ → C(Seq ι (κ ⊕ ι), ℝ),
      (∀ i a, P i a ∈ attentionAlgebra ι (κ ⊕ ι)) ∧
      (∀ i a, Invariant (fun z => P i a z)) ∧
      ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ i a, |P i a (posEnc x) - F x i a| < eps := by
  choose P hP hPinv hclose using fun (i : ι) (a : κ) =>
    positional_restores_universality (ι := ι) (κ := κ) ⟨fun x => F x i a, hF i a⟩ hK heps
  exact ⟨P, hP, hPinv, fun x hx i a => hclose i a x hx⟩

end PositionalRepair

section EquivariantHeads

variable {ι κ : Type*} [DecidableEq ι]

/-- The marked-query encoding: the queried position `i` is flagged by an extra feature. -/
def markAt (i : ι) (x : Seq ι κ) : Seq ι (κ ⊕ Unit) :=
  fun j => Sum.elim (x j) (fun _ => if j = i then (1:ℝ) else 0)

theorem markAt_permAct (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) (i : ι) (x : Seq ι κ) :
    markAt i (permAct σ x) = permAct σ (markAt (σ i) x) := by
  funext j c
  cases c with
  | inl a => rfl
  | inr _ =>
      show (if j = i then (1:ℝ) else 0) = if σ j = σ i then (1:ℝ) else 0
      by_cases h : j = i
      · simp [h]
      · simp [h]

/-- **Marked invariant functionals are exactly equivariant heads.**  If `G` is invariant under a
token symmetry `σ`, then the head `i ↦ G (markAt i x)` is `σ`-equivariant: permuting the input
tokens permutes the outputs, which is the symmetry a positional-encoding-free transformer layer
possesses. -/
theorem marked_head_equivariant {G : Seq ι (κ ⊕ Unit) → ℝ} {σ : Equiv.Perm ι}
    (hG : ∀ z, G (permAct σ z) = G z) (i : ι) (x : Seq ι κ) :
    G (markAt i (permAct σ x)) = G (markAt (σ i) x) := by
  rw [markAt_permAct, hG]

end EquivariantHeads

section EquivariantUniversality

variable {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ]
variable {Γ : Type*} [Group Γ] [Fintype Γ]

/-- The feature block of an augmented (marked) sequence. -/
def feat (z : Seq ι (κ ⊕ Unit)) : Seq ι κ := fun i a => z i (Sum.inl a)

/-- The mark coordinate of an augmented sequence. -/
def markCoord (z : Seq ι (κ ⊕ Unit)) (i : ι) : ℝ := z i (Sum.inr ())

/-- A sequence-to-sequence map is *`Γ`-equivariant* when a token symmetry of the input permutes
the output tokens the same way. -/
def EquivariantUnder (act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι) (F : Seq ι κ → Seq ι κ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Γ) (x : Seq ι κ) (i : ι) (a : κ), F (permAct (act g) x) i a = F x (act g i) a

/-- The *marked functional* of an equivariant map: contract the output of `F` on the feature
block against the mark coordinates.  This is the key construction: it converts an equivariant
sequence-to-sequence map into a genuinely **invariant** scalar functional of the marked
sequence, with no loss of information. -/
def markedFunctional (F : Seq ι κ → Seq ι κ) (a : κ) (z : Seq ι (κ ⊕ Unit)) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, F (feat z) i a * markCoord z i

omit [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ] in
theorem feat_permAct (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) (z : Seq ι (κ ⊕ Unit)) :
    feat (permAct σ z) = permAct σ (feat z) := rfl

omit [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ] [Fintype Γ] in
/-- **Equivariance becomes invariance after marking.** -/
theorem markedFunctional_invariant {act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι} {F : Seq ι κ → Seq ι κ}
    (hF : EquivariantUnder act F) (a : κ) :
    InvariantUnder act (markedFunctional F a) := by
  intro gamma z
  show ∑ i, F (feat (permAct (act gamma) z)) i a * markCoord (permAct (act gamma) z) i
      = ∑ i, F (feat z) i a * markCoord z i
  rw [feat_permAct]
  have hstep : ∀ i : ι, F (permAct (act gamma) (feat z)) i a * markCoord (permAct (act gamma) z) i
      = F (feat z) (act gamma i) a * markCoord z (act gamma i) := by
    intro i
    rw [hF gamma (feat z) i a]
    rfl
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => hstep i)]
  exact Equiv.sum_comp (act gamma) (fun i => F (feat z) i a * markCoord z i)

omit [Fintype κ] in
/-- The marked functional reproduces `F` exactly on marked sequences. -/
theorem markedFunctional_markAt (F : Seq ι κ → Seq ι κ) (a : κ) (i : ι) (x : Seq ι κ) :
    markedFunctional F a (markAt i x) = F x i a := by
  have hfeat : feat (markAt i x) = x := rfl
  show ∑ i', F (feat (markAt i x)) i' a * markCoord (markAt i x) i' = F x i a
  rw [hfeat]
  have hmark : ∀ i' : ι, markCoord (markAt i x) i' = if i' = i then (1:ℝ) else 0 := fun _ => rfl
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i' _ => by rw [hmark i'])]
  rw [Finset.sum_eq_single i]
  · simp
  · intro i' _ hi'; simp [hi']
  · intro h; exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ i) h

omit [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ] in
theorem continuous_markedFunctional {F : Seq ι κ → Seq ι κ}
    (hF : ∀ i a, Continuous fun x => F x i a) (a : κ) :
    Continuous (markedFunctional F a) := by
  apply continuous_finset_sum
  intro i _
  have hfeat : Continuous (feat (ι := ι) (κ := κ)) := by
    apply continuous_pi; intro m; apply continuous_pi; intro b
    exact (continuous_apply (Sum.inl b)).comp (continuous_apply m)
  have h1 : Continuous fun z : Seq ι (κ ⊕ Unit) => F (feat z) i a := (hF i a).comp hfeat
  have h2 : Continuous fun z : Seq ι (κ ⊕ Unit) => markCoord z i :=
    (continuous_apply (Sum.inr ())).comp (continuous_apply i)
  exact h1.mul h2

omit [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] in
theorem continuous_markAt (i : ι) : Continuous (markAt (κ := κ) i) := by
  apply continuous_pi; intro j; apply continuous_pi; intro c
  cases c with
  | inl a => exact (continuous_apply a).comp (continuous_apply j)
  | inr _ => exact continuous_const

/-- The symmetry saturation of the marked image of a set of sequences. -/
def markSaturation (act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι) (K : Set (Seq ι κ)) : Set (Seq ι (κ ⊕ Unit)) :=
  ⋃ g : Γ, ⋃ i : ι, (permAct (act g)) '' (markAt i '' K)

omit [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] [Fintype Γ] in
theorem markAt_mem_markSaturation (act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι) {K : Set (Seq ι κ)} {x : Seq ι κ}
    (hx : x ∈ K) (i : ι) : markAt i x ∈ markSaturation act K :=
  Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨1, Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨i, ⟨markAt i x, ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩, by simp⟩⟩⟩

omit [Fintype κ] in
theorem isCompact_markSaturation (act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι) {K : Set (Seq ι κ)}
    (hK : IsCompact K) : IsCompact (markSaturation act K) :=
  isCompact_iUnion fun g =>
    isCompact_iUnion fun i => ((hK.image (continuous_markAt i)).image (continuous_permAct (act g)))

omit [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] [Fintype Γ] in
theorem saturated_markSaturation (act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι) (K : Set (Seq ι κ)) :
    SaturatedUnder act (markSaturation act K) := by
  rintro tau z hz
  rw [markSaturation, Set.mem_iUnion] at hz ⊢
  obtain ⟨gamma, hz⟩ := hz
  rw [Set.mem_iUnion] at hz
  obtain ⟨i, w, hw, rfl⟩ := hz
  refine ⟨gamma * tau, ?_⟩
  rw [Set.mem_iUnion]
  refine ⟨i, w, hw, ?_⟩
  rw [MonoidHom.map_mul]
  exact (permAct_comp (act tau) (act gamma) w).symm ▸ rfl

/-- **Equivariant universality: the exact converse of the symmetry barrier.**
A `Γ`-invariant attention model, queried through the marked encoding, uniformly approximates
*every* continuous `Γ`-equivariant sequence-to-sequence map on every compact domain — and the
resulting head family is itself exactly `Γ`-equivariant.

Together with `symmetry_barrier_position_read` (no invariant model can approximate a
non-equivariant target) and `positional_restores_universality` (positional encodings remove the
restriction), this pins down the expressive power of symmetric attention: it is precisely the
equivariant continuous maps. -/
theorem equivariant_uniform_universal (act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι) (F : Seq ι κ → Seq ι κ)
    (hFc : ∀ i a, Continuous fun x => F x i a) (hFe : EquivariantUnder act F)
    {K : Set (Seq ι κ)} (hK : IsCompact K) {eps : ℝ} (heps : 0 < eps) :
    ∃ P : κ → C(Seq ι (κ ⊕ Unit), ℝ),
      (∀ a, P a ∈ attentionAlgebra ι (κ ⊕ Unit)) ∧
      (∀ a, InvariantUnder act (fun z => P a z)) ∧
      (∀ (a : κ) (g : Γ) (i : ι) (x : Seq ι κ),
        P a (markAt i (permAct (act g) x)) = P a (markAt (act g i) x)) ∧
      (∀ x ∈ K, ∀ i a, |P a (markAt i x) - F x i a| < eps) := by
  have hstep : ∀ a : κ, ∃ p ∈ attentionAlgebra ι (κ ⊕ Unit),
      InvariantUnder act (fun z => p z) ∧
        ∀ z ∈ markSaturation act K, |p z - markedFunctional F a z| < eps := by
    intro a
    exact group_uniform_universal (ι := ι) (κ := κ ⊕ Unit) act
      ⟨markedFunctional F a, continuous_markedFunctional hFc a⟩
      (markedFunctional_invariant hFe a) (isCompact_markSaturation act hK)
      (saturated_markSaturation act K) heps
  choose P hPmem hPinv hPclose using hstep
  refine ⟨P, hPmem, hPinv, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro a g i x
    exact marked_head_equivariant (fun z => hPinv a g z) i x
  · intro x hx i a
    have h := hPclose a (markAt i x) (markAt_mem_markSaturation act hx i)
    rwa [markedFunctional_markAt] at h

omit [Fintype κ] [Fintype Γ] in
/-- **Representation theorem for equivariant sequence-to-sequence maps.**  A continuous map is
`Γ`-equivariant if and only if it is the marked evaluation of a family of continuous
`Γ`-**invariant** functionals.  Equivariance and invariance are therefore the same data, read
through the marked-token encoding; this is the structural reason `equivariant_uniform_universal`
follows from `group_uniform_universal`. -/
theorem equivariant_iff_exists_marked_invariant (act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι)
    (F : Seq ι κ → Seq ι κ) :
    ((∀ i a, Continuous fun x => F x i a) ∧ EquivariantUnder act F)
      ↔ ∃ G : κ → C(Seq ι (κ ⊕ Unit), ℝ),
          (∀ a, InvariantUnder act (fun z => G a z)) ∧
            ∀ x i a, F x i a = G a (markAt i x) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hFc, hFe⟩
    refine ⟨fun a => ⟨markedFunctional F a, continuous_markedFunctional hFc a⟩,
      fun a => markedFunctional_invariant hFe a, ?_⟩
    intro x i a
    exact (markedFunctional_markAt F a i x).symm
  · rintro ⟨G, hGinv, hGF⟩
    constructor
    · intro i a
      have : (fun x => F x i a) = fun x => G a (markAt i x) := by
        funext x; exact hGF x i a
      rw [this]
      exact (G a).continuous.comp (continuous_markAt i)
    · intro g x i a
      rw [hGF (permAct (act g) x) i a, hGF x (act g i) a]
      exact marked_head_equivariant (fun z => hGinv a g z) i x

/-- **Full permutation equivariance.**  Specialization of `equivariant_uniform_universal` to the
whole symmetric group: positional-encoding-free attention is a universal approximator of the
continuous permutation-equivariant sequence-to-sequence maps. -/
theorem symmetric_equivariant_universal (F : Seq ι κ → Seq ι κ)
    (hFc : ∀ i a, Continuous fun x => F x i a)
    (hFe : ∀ (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) (x : Seq ι κ) (i : ι) (a : κ),
      F (permAct σ x) i a = F x (σ i) a)
    {K : Set (Seq ι κ)} (hK : IsCompact K) {eps : ℝ} (heps : 0 < eps) :
    ∃ P : κ → C(Seq ι (κ ⊕ Unit), ℝ),
      (∀ a, P a ∈ attentionAlgebra ι (κ ⊕ Unit)) ∧
      (∀ a, Invariant (fun z => P a z)) ∧
      (∀ (a : κ) (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) (i : ι) (x : Seq ι κ),
        P a (markAt i (permAct σ x)) = P a (markAt (σ i) x)) ∧
      (∀ x ∈ K, ∀ i a, |P a (markAt i x) - F x i a| < eps) :=
  equivariant_uniform_universal (MonoidHom.id (Equiv.Perm ι)) F hFc hFe hK heps

end EquivariantUniversality

end PermutationDichotomy
d255762b-4bf4-46b6-9ab5-efc46c515cf9.result_demo:
"""
Numerical demonstrations of the symmetry dichotomy for attention architectures.

The mathematics being illustrated
---------------------------------
A *sequence* is an n-by-d real table x, with x[i][a] the a-th feature of token i.
A token permutation sigma acts by  (sigma . x)[i] = x[sigma(i)].

A *readout* with weight table w is the linear functional

        R_w(x) = sum_i sum_a w[i][a] * x[i][a],

which is exactly a softmax attention head whose scores are all equal (uniform
attention), up to the factor 1/n absorbed into w.  The *attention algebra* A is
the algebra of real polynomials in readouts: sums model multi-head attention,
products model the multiplicative interaction generated by stacking layers.

The results demonstrated below:

  D1  Uniform-score softmax heads ARE readouts.
  D2  Position-reading barrier: any permutation-invariant model errs by >= 1/2
      when asked to report an absolute coordinate.
  D3  Orbit barrier equality: the optimal invariant error on an orbit is
      EXACTLY half the orbit oscillation, attained by the orbit midpoint.
  D4  Averaging is free: symmetrizing an approximant of an invariant target
      never increases the uniform error (and usually decreases it).
  D5  Symmetric universality: invariant elements of the attention algebra
      approximate an invariant target to any accuracy, with error decreasing
      as the polynomial degree grows.
  D6  Positional repair: the one-hot encoding admits a permutation-INVARIANT
      quadratic decoder that inverts it, so invariant models regain the ability
      to read absolute positions.
  D7  Equivariance = marked invariance: the marked functional of an equivariant
      map is invariant and reproduces the map exactly.

Requires only the Python standard library and NumPy.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
from typing import Callable, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

import numpy as np

Array = np.ndarray
Perm = Tuple[int, ...]


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Core objects: the token action, readouts, softmax heads
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def act(sigma: Perm, x: Array) -> Array:
    """Token action: (sigma . x)[i] = x[sigma(i)].  x has shape (n, d)."""
    return x[list(sigma), :]


def all_perms(n: int) -> List[Perm]:
    """The full symmetric group on {0, ..., n-1}."""
    return list(itertools.permutations(range(n)))


def cyclic_group(n: int) -> List[Perm]:
    """The cyclic shift group generated by i -> i+1 mod n."""
    return [tuple((i + k) % n for i in range(n)) for k in range(n)]


def readout(w: Array, x: Array) -> float:
    """R_w(x) = sum_i sum_a w[i,a] x[i,a]."""
    return float(np.sum(w * x))


def softmax_head(scores: Array, w: Array, x: Array) -> float:
    """A genuine softmax attention head: softmax(scores) . (row-wise w-values)."""
    e = np.exp(scores - np.max(scores))
    alpha = e / np.sum(e)
    values = np.sum(w * x, axis=1)
    return float(np.dot(alpha, values))


def demo_1_heads_are_readouts() -> None:
    print("D1  Uniform-score softmax heads are exactly readouts")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    n, d = 4, 3
    w = rng.normal(size=(n, d))
    x = rng.normal(size=(n, d))
    lhs = softmax_head(np.zeros(n), w, x)
    rhs = readout(w / n, x)
    print(f"    softmax head with zero scores : {lhs: .10f}")
    print(f"    readout with weights w/n      : {rhs: .10f}")
    print(f"    agree to 1e-12                : {abs(lhs - rhs) < 1e-12}")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# D2 / D3: the sharp barrier
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def orbit(group: Sequence[Perm], x: Array) -> List[Array]:
    return [act(s, x) for s in group]


def orbit_barrier(target: Callable[[Array], float],
                  x: Array,
                  group: Sequence[Perm]) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """Return (optimal invariant error on the orbit of x, optimal model value).

    Theory: an invariant model is constant on the orbit, so the best it can do
    is the midpoint of the range of the target over the orbit, and the error is
    exactly half the oscillation.
    """
    vals = [target(y) for y in orbit(group, x)]
    hi, lo = max(vals), min(vals)
    return (hi - lo) / 2.0, (hi + lo) / 2.0


def demo_2_position_barrier() -> None:
    print("D2  Position-reading barrier: reading token 0 costs at least 1/2")
    n, d = 2, 1
    group = all_perms(n)
    target = lambda y: float(y[0, 0])          # "report the first coordinate"

    # The witness from the proof: the one-hot table u with u[0,0] = 1.
    u = np.zeros((n, d))
    u[0, 0] = 1.0
    err, best = orbit_barrier(target, u, group)
    print(f"    orbit of the one-hot witness : "
          f"{[float(t[0, 0]) for t in orbit(group, u)]}")
    print(f"    best invariant constant      : {best:.4f}")
    print(f"    optimal error                : {err:.4f}   (theory: 0.5)")

    # Brute-force check over a rich family of invariant models: every symmetric
    # polynomial of degree <= 3 in the two coordinates, fitted by least squares.
    grid = np.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, 41)
    pts = np.array([[p, q] for p in grid for q in grid])
    feats = np.stack([
        np.ones(len(pts)),
        pts[:, 0] + pts[:, 1],
        pts[:, 0] * pts[:, 1],
        pts[:, 0] ** 2 + pts[:, 1] ** 2,
        (pts[:, 0] + pts[:, 1]) ** 3,
        pts[:, 0] ** 2 * pts[:, 1] + pts[:, 0] * pts[:, 1] ** 2,
    ], axis=1)                                  # all columns are symmetric
    y = pts[:, 0]                               # target = first coordinate
    coef, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(feats, y, rcond=None)
    sup_err = float(np.max(np.abs(feats @ coef - y)))
    print(f"    best symmetric cubic fit, sup error on the grid : {sup_err:.4f}")
    print(f"    exceeds the 1/2 barrier                         : {sup_err >= 0.5 - 1e-9}")
    print()


def demo_3_orbit_equality() -> None:
    print("D3  Orbit barrier is an EQUALITY: optimal error = oscillation / 2")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
    n, d = 3, 2
    group = all_perms(n)
    # A deliberately order-sensitive target.
    target = lambda y: float(y[0, 0] + 2.0 * y[1, 1] - y[2, 0] ** 2)

    for trial in range(3):
        x = rng.normal(size=(n, d))
        err, best = orbit_barrier(target, x, group)
        vals = [target(y) for y in orbit(group, x)]
        osc = max(vals) - min(vals)
        # Achievability: the constant midpoint model, evaluated on the orbit.
        attained = max(abs(best - v) for v in vals)
        # Lower bound: no invariant model (i.e. no constant on the orbit) beats it.
        sweep = min(max(abs(c - v) for v in vals)
                    for c in np.linspace(min(vals) - 1, max(vals) + 1, 20001))
        print(f"    trial {trial}: osc/2 = {osc / 2:.6f} | midpoint attains "
              f"{attained:.6f} | best over all constants {sweep:.6f}")
    print("    -> lower bound and achievability coincide.")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# D4 / D5: the positive half
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def monomial_exponents(n_feats: int, degree: int) -> List[Tuple[int, ...]]:
    """All exponent vectors of total degree <= `degree` over `n_feats` readouts."""
    out: List[Tuple[int, ...]] = []
    for total in range(degree + 1):
        for combo in itertools.combinations_with_replacement(range(n_feats), total):
            e = [0] * n_feats
            for c in combo:
                e[c] += 1
            out.append(tuple(e))
    return out


def attention_features(x: Array, weights: Sequence[Array],
                       exps: Sequence[Tuple[int, ...]]) -> Array:
    """Evaluate the monomials in the readouts R_{w_1}, ..., R_{w_m} at x.

    Each returned coordinate is an element of the attention algebra.
    """
    base = np.array([readout(w, x) for w in weights])
    return np.array([float(np.prod(base ** np.array(e))) for e in exps])


def symmetrize(model: Callable[[Array], float],
               group: Sequence[Perm]) -> Callable[[Array], float]:
    """Group averaging: S_G f (x) = (1/|G|) sum_g f(g . x)."""
    def averaged(x: Array) -> float:
        return float(np.mean([model(act(s, x)) for s in group]))
    return averaged


def demo_4_averaging_is_free() -> None:
    print("D4  Averaging is free: symmetrizing never hurts on an invariant target")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
    n, d = 3, 2
    group = all_perms(n)
    # An invariant target: a symmetric function of the tokens.
    target = lambda y: float(np.sum(np.sum(y, axis=1) ** 2))

    weights = [rng.normal(size=(n, d)) for _ in range(4)]
    exps = monomial_exponents(len(weights), degree=2)

    # A deliberately ASYMMETRIC fit: train only on unsaturated samples.
    train = [rng.normal(size=(n, d)) for _ in range(400)]
    A = np.stack([attention_features(x, weights, exps) for x in train])
    b = np.array([target(x) for x in train])
    coef, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, b, rcond=None)
    raw = lambda x: float(np.dot(coef, attention_features(x, weights, exps)))
    sym = symmetrize(raw, group)

    test = [rng.normal(size=(n, d)) for _ in range(300)]
    saturated = [act(s, x) for x in test for s in group]
    e_raw = max(abs(raw(x) - target(x)) for x in saturated)
    e_sym = max(abs(sym(x) - target(x)) for x in saturated)
    print(f"    sup error, unsymmetrized model : {e_raw:.6f}")
    print(f"    sup error, symmetrized model   : {e_sym:.6f}")
    print(f"    symmetrization did not hurt    : {e_sym <= e_raw + 1e-9}")
    print(f"    symmetrized model is invariant : "
          f"{max(abs(sym(act(s, test[0])) - sym(test[0])) for s in group) < 1e-9}")
    print()


def demo_5_symmetric_universality() -> None:
    print("D5  Symmetric universality: error shrinks as the algebra degree grows")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(11)
    n, d = 3, 2
    group = all_perms(n)
    # Invariant, genuinely nonlinear target: a multisymmetric power sum mixture.
    def target(y: Array) -> float:
        return float(np.sum(y[:, 0] ** 2 * y[:, 1]) + np.sum(np.tanh(y[:, 1])))

    # Coordinate readouts span all linear functionals; symmetrized monomials in
    # them span the invariant part of the attention algebra degree by degree.
    weights: List[Array] = []
    for i in range(n):
        for a in range(d):
            w = np.zeros((n, d))
            w[i, a] = 1.0
            weights.append(w)

    train = [rng.normal(scale=0.5, size=(n, d)) for _ in range(2000)]
    test = [rng.normal(scale=0.5, size=(n, d)) for _ in range(300)]

    for degree in (1, 2, 3, 4, 5):
        exps = monomial_exponents(len(weights), degree)
        def feats(x: Array, exps: Sequence[Tuple[int, ...]] = exps) -> Array:
            # symmetrized features: average the monomials over the group
            return np.mean([attention_features(act(s, x), weights, exps)
                            for s in group], axis=0)
        A = np.stack([feats(x) for x in train])
        b = np.array([target(x) for x in train])
        # Column rescaling keeps the (badly conditioned) monomial basis usable.
        scale = np.maximum(np.sqrt(np.mean(A ** 2, axis=0)), 1e-12)
        coef, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A / scale, b, rcond=1e-10)
        errs = [abs(float(np.dot(coef, feats(x) / scale)) - target(x))
                for x in test]
        rms = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(np.square(errs))))
        print(f"    degree {degree}: #invariant features = {len(exps):4d} | "
              f"sup error = {max(errs):.6f} | rms error = {rms:.6f}")
    print("    -> density of the invariant part of the attention algebra.")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# D6: positional encoding and the invariant decoder
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def pos_encode(x: Array) -> Array:
    """One-hot positional encoding: append the indicator of the token's index."""
    n, _ = x.shape
    return np.concatenate([x, np.eye(n)], axis=1)


def invariant_decode(z: Array, n_feats: int) -> Array:
    """dec(z)[i,a] = sum_j z[j, pos(i)] * z[j, feat(a)] -- one attention pattern.

    This is a sum over tokens, hence permutation-invariant, yet it inverts the
    one-hot positional encoding exactly.
    """
    feats = z[:, :n_feats]
    tags = z[:, n_feats:]
    return tags.T @ feats


def demo_6_positional_repair() -> None:
    print("D6  Positional repair: an invariant quadratic decoder inverts the encoding")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(5)
    n, d = 4, 3
    x = rng.normal(size=(n, d))
    z = pos_encode(x)
    print(f"    ||dec(enc(x)) - x||_inf                    : "
          f"{np.max(np.abs(invariant_decode(z, d) - x)):.2e}")
    worst = 0.0
    for s in all_perms(n):
        worst = max(worst, float(np.max(np.abs(
            invariant_decode(act(s, z), d) - invariant_decode(z, d)))))
    print(f"    max change of dec under all n! permutations: {worst:.2e}")
    print("    -> the decoder is exactly permutation-invariant AND inverts enc,")
    print("       so invariant models on encoded input read absolute positions.")

    # Concretely: an invariant model on encoded input recovers x[0,0] exactly,
    # which by D2 is impossible without the encoding.
    read_first = lambda zz: float(invariant_decode(zz, d)[0, 0])
    errs = [abs(read_first(act(s, z)) - x[0, 0]) for s in all_perms(n)]
    print(f"    invariant read of x[0,0] on encoded input, max error over the")
    print(f"    whole orbit: {max(errs):.2e}   (barrier without encoding: 0.5)")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# D7: equivariance = marked invariance
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def mark_at(i: int, x: Array) -> Array:
    """Marked-token encoding: append a single feature flagging position i."""
    n, _ = x.shape
    flag = np.zeros((n, 1))
    flag[i, 0] = 1.0
    return np.concatenate([x, flag], axis=1)


def marked_functional(F: Callable[[Array], Array], a: int, z: Array) -> float:
    """G_a(z) = sum_i F(feat(z))[i,a] * mark(z)[i]."""
    feats = z[:, :-1]
    mark = z[:, -1]
    return float(np.dot(F(feats)[:, a], mark))


def demo_7_equivariance_is_marked_invariance() -> None:
    print("D7  Equivariance = invariance, seen through the marked-token window")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(13)
    n, d = 3, 2
    group = all_perms(n)

    # A permutation-equivariant sequence-to-sequence map: each token's output
    # depends on its own features and on order-free statistics of the whole set.
    def F(x: Array) -> Array:
        pooled = np.sum(x, axis=0, keepdims=True)
        return np.tanh(x) + 0.3 * x * pooled

    x = rng.normal(size=(n, d))

    # (a) F really is equivariant.
    eq = max(float(np.max(np.abs(F(act(s, x)) - act(s, F(x))))) for s in group)
    print(f"    equivariance defect of F                : {eq:.2e}")

    # (b) The marked functional is invariant ...
    z = mark_at(1, x)
    inv = max(abs(marked_functional(F, 0, act(s, z)) - marked_functional(F, 0, z))
              for s in group)
    print(f"    invariance defect of the marked functional: {inv:.2e}")

    # (c) ... and reproduces F exactly on marked sequences.
    rep = max(abs(marked_functional(F, a, mark_at(i, x)) - F(x)[i, a])
              for i in range(n) for a in range(d))
    print(f"    ||G_a(mark_i(x)) - F(x)[i,a]||_inf        : {rep:.2e}")

    # (d) The induced head family is EXACTLY equivariant, not approximately.
    head_defect = max(
        abs(marked_functional(F, a, mark_at(i, act(s, x)))
            - marked_functional(F, a, mark_at(s[i], x)))
        for s in group for i in range(n) for a in range(d))
    print(f"    exact equivariance of the head family     : {head_defect:.2e}")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bonus: the cyclic (relative-encoding) regime inherits the same barrier
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_8_relative_encoding_barrier() -> None:
    print("D8  Relative (cyclic) symmetry inherits the 1/2 absolute-position barrier")
    n, d = 5, 1
    group = cyclic_group(n)
    u = np.zeros((n, d))
    u[0, 0] = 1.0
    target = lambda y: float(y[0, 0])
    err, best = orbit_barrier(target, u, group)
    print(f"    cyclic orbit values of 'read token 0' : "
          f"{[float(t[0, 0]) for t in orbit(group, u)]}")
    print(f"    optimal shift-invariant error         : {err:.4f}  (theory: 0.5)")

    # But a SHIFT-INVARIANT target is approximated perfectly by a shift-invariant
    # model: the barrier is exactly the failure of invariance, nothing more.
    rng = np.random.default_rng(21)
    x = rng.normal(size=(n, d))
    shift_inv_target = lambda y: float(np.sum(y[:, 0] * np.roll(y[:, 0], 1)))
    err2, _ = orbit_barrier(shift_inv_target, x, group)
    print(f"    optimal error for a shift-INVARIANT target: {err2:.2e}")
    print()


def main() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("The symmetry dichotomy for attention architectures -- numerical demos")
    print("=" * 78)
    print()
    demo_1_heads_are_readouts()
    demo_2_position_barrier()
    demo_3_orbit_equality()
    demo_4_averaging_is_free()
    demo_5_symmetric_universality()
    demo_6_positional_repair()
    demo_7_equivariance_is_marked_invariance()
    demo_8_relative_encoding_barrier()
    print("=" * 78)
    print("Summary: symmetric attention is dense in the invariant continuous")
    print("functionals and confined to them; the cost outside is exactly half the")
    print("orbit oscillation; one-hot positional tags remove the cost entirely")
    print("without breaking the model's symmetry; and in the sequence-to-sequence")
    print("setting the reach is exactly the continuous equivariant maps.")
    print("=" * 78)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Computational evidence for the symmetry dichotomy of attention architectures

All numbers below were produced by exact rational (`ℚ`) computation in Lean 4 (`#eval`) before
the formal proofs in
`Catalog/MachineLearning/TransformerUniversality/PermutationDichotomy.lean` were written.  They
are *evidence*, not verification; every claim that appears as a theorem in the catalog is proved
there with 0 sorries.

## 1. Group averaging collapses readouts to uniform pooling

Symmetrizing the weight vector `w` of a linear attention readout over all 6 permutations of a
3-token sequence (`symW w = (1/6) ∑_σ w ∘ σ`):

| input `w`  | symmetrized weights |
|------------|---------------------|
| `[1,0,0]`  | `[1/3, 1/3, 1/3]`   |
| `[2,0,0]`  | `[2/3, 2/3, 2/3]`   |
| `[1,2,3]`  | `[2, 2, 2]`         |

Observation that shaped the formalization: the symmetrization of a *single* readout is always a
uniform-attention (mean-pooling) readout, i.e. the linear part of the symmetric class is only
one-dimensional per feature.  Hence the invariant class can only be rich because of the
*multiplicative* (feed-forward / gating) structure of the algebra — this is why the positive
half of the dichotomy is proved for the subalgebra `attentionAlgebra`, not for readouts alone,
and why the averaging step is applied *after* Stone–Weierstrass rather than before.
Formal counterparts: `symmetrize_mem`, `symmetrize_invariant`, `softmaxHeadRead_zero_scores`.

## 2. The orbit barrier is exactly 1/2 for position reading

Target `g x = x 0` (read the first token), input `u = (1,0,0)`, orbit under `S_3`:

* values of `g` on the orbit: `[1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0]`;
* half oscillation `(max − min)/2 = 1/2`;
* errors of the best invariant (constant midpoint `1/2`) model on the orbit:
  `[1/2, 1/2, 1/2, 1/2, 1/2, 1/2]`.

So the lower bound `1/2` is met with equality by a constant model: the barrier is *sharp*, not
merely a bound.  Formal counterparts: `orbit_barrier_lower`, `orbit_barrier_attained`,
`symmetry_barrier_position_read`.

## 3. Relative (cyclic) symmetry has the same barrier

For a 4-token sequence with the cyclic shift `r` and `u = (1,0,0,0)`, the values of `g x = x 0`
along the cyclic orbit are `[1, 0, 0, 0]`: oscillation 1, barrier `1/2` again.  A shift-invariant
(relative positional encoding) model is therefore just as unable to read an *absolute* position
as a fully permutation-symmetric one.  This suggested proving the barrier for a *single*
permutation that moves the queried position, which is the form
`symmetry_barrier_position_read` actually takes, and motivated generalizing the positive half
from `S_ι` to an arbitrary finite symmetry group (`group_uniform_universal`,
`shift_uniform_universal`).

## 4. Counterexample hunt

We looked for an invariant functional separating two sequences that differ only by a
permutation; by construction none exists, and the search instead produced the two-point
certificate `u = (1,0,…,0)` versus `σ · u` used in the Lean proof.  No counterexample to any
stated theorem was found; the one *failed* conjecture of the cycle (that linear readouts alone,
without the multiplicative mixing, already give the symmetric universality) is refuted by
table 1 above: symmetrized readouts span a one-dimensional space per feature, so they cannot
approximate, e.g., the invariant functional `x ↦ ∑_i (x_i)²`.

## 5. No OEIS sequence

No integer sequence arises in this development (the objects are function algebras and
approximation constants), so no OEIS lookup applies.

# Future directions: bold, testable conjectures from the symmetry dichotomy

The cycle established, in
`Catalog/MachineLearning/TransformerUniversality/PermutationDichotomy.lean` (0 sorries):

* `group_uniform_universal` — for **any** finite group `Γ` of token symmetries, the
  `Γ`-invariant part of the attention algebra is uniformly dense in the `Γ`-invariant continuous
  functionals on compact saturated domains (specializations: `symmetric_uniform_universal` for
  the full symmetric group, `shift_uniform_universal` for cyclic/relative symmetry);
* `equivariant_uniform_universal` — the exact converse in the sequence-to-sequence setting:
  symmetric attention, queried through the marked-token encoding, is a universal approximator of
  the continuous `Γ`-equivariant maps, and the constructed heads are exactly equivariant;
* `equivariant_iff_exists_marked_invariant` — a representation theorem: continuous equivariant
  sequence-to-sequence maps are *exactly* the marked-token evaluations of continuous invariant
  functionals;
* `orbit_barrier_lower` / `orbit_barrier_attained` / `symmetry_barrier_position_read` — the
  obstruction is *sharp*: the optimal invariant error on an orbit equals exactly half the orbit
  oscillation, and reading an absolute position costs at least `1/2`;
* `positional_restores_universality` / `positional_seq2seq_universality` — one-hot positional
  encodings remove the obstruction completely, via an explicit invariant continuous decoder.

Below are the follow-up conjectures, ranked by expected impact.

## C1. Head-count law: the symmetric approximant needs only orbit-many heads, not `|Γ|`-many

**Conjecture.** For every `Γ`-invariant `g ∈ C(K, ℝ)` and `ε > 0`, there is a `Γ`-invariant
element of `attentionAlgebra` that `ε`-approximates `g` and is a sum of at most
`poly(dim, 1/ε)` products of readouts — in particular independent of `|Γ| = n!`, which is what
the averaging proof of `group_uniform_universal` currently spends.

*The key insight is* that averaging over `Γ` is a *projection*, not a construction: the invariant
subalgebra is already generated by the multisymmetric power sums `x ↦ ∑_i ∏_a (x_i a)^{e_a}`,
each of which is a **single** product of readouts, so the group sum can be eliminated in favour
of a generating set of size polynomial in the feature dimension and the degree.

*Why now?* The stability lemma `attentionAlgebra_compPerm_mem` plus the sharp barrier give both
halves needed to measure such a bound: any candidate generating set can be tested against the
`1/2` barrier of `symmetry_barrier_position_read`, so the conjecture is falsifiable by an
explicit finite computation at small `|ι|`.

## C2. Softmax realizability: every element of the attention algebra is a limit of genuine
softmax transformer blocks

**Conjecture.** The uniform closure on compacta of finite compositions of *softmax* attention
