  classical
  haveI : Fintype (Subgroup.zpowers r) := Fintype.ofFinite _
  have hpow : ∀ s : Subgroup.zpowers r, ∃ k : ℕ, r ^ k = (s : Equiv.Perm ι) := by
    intro s
    have hs : (s : Equiv.Perm ι) ∈ Subgroup.zpowers r := s.2
    rw [← mem_powers_iff_mem_zpowers] at hs
    obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hs
    exact ⟨k, hk⟩
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpinv, hclose⟩ :=
    group_uniform_universal (Γ := Subgroup.zpowers r) (Subgroup.zpowers r).subtype g
      (by
        intro s x
        obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hpow s
        show g (permAct (s : Equiv.Perm ι) x) = g x
        rw [← hk]
        exact hg k x)
      hK
      (by
        intro s x hx
        obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hpow s
        show permAct (s : Equiv.Perm ι) x ∈ K
        rw [← hk]
        exact hKsat k x hx)
      heps
  refine ⟨p, hp, ?_, hclose⟩
  intro k x
  exact hpinv ⟨r ^ k, Subgroup.mem_zpowers_iff.mpr ⟨(k : ℤ), by simp⟩⟩ x

end PositiveHalf

section NegativeHalf

variable {ι κ : Type*}

/-- **The invariance defect is an approximation barrier.**  Any model invariant under a single
token permutation `σ` pays, somewhere on the `σ`-orbit, at least half of the target's defect
along `σ`. -/
theorem invariant_defect_lower_bound {p g : Seq ι κ → ℝ} {σ : Equiv.Perm ι}
    (hp : ∀ x, p (permAct σ x) = p x) (x : Seq ι κ) :
    |g x - g (permAct σ x)| ≤ |p x - g x| + |p (permAct σ x) - g (permAct σ x)| := by
  have h : g x - g (permAct σ x)
      = -(p x - g x) + (p (permAct σ x) - g (permAct σ x)) := by
    rw [hp x]; ring
  calc |g x - g (permAct σ x)|
      ≤ |-(p x - g x)| + |p (permAct σ x) - g (permAct σ x)| := by
        rw [h]; exact abs_add_le _ _
    _ = |p x - g x| + |p (permAct σ x) - g (permAct σ x)| := by rw [abs_neg]

/-- **The symmetric class is uniformly closed.**  A functional approximated to arbitrary
accuracy by `σ`-invariant models on a `σ`-stable set is itself `σ`-invariant there. -/
theorem symmetric_class_closed_under_uniform_limits {g : Seq ι κ → ℝ} {K : Set (Seq ι κ)}
    {σ : Equiv.Perm ι} (hKsat : ∀ x ∈ K, permAct σ x ∈ K)
    (h : ∀ eps > 0, ∃ p : Seq ι κ → ℝ,
      (∀ y, p (permAct σ y) = p y) ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, |p x - g x| < eps)
    (x : Seq ι κ) (hx : x ∈ K) :
    g (permAct σ x) = g x := by
  have hzero : g x - g (permAct σ x) = 0 := by
    by_contra hne
    have hd : 0 < |g x - g (permAct σ x)| := abs_pos.mpr hne
    obtain ⟨p, hp, hclose⟩ := h (|g x - g (permAct σ x)| / 4) (by linarith)
    have h1 := hclose x hx
    have h2 := hclose (permAct σ x) (hKsat x hx)
    have h3 := invariant_defect_lower_bound (g := g) hp x
    linarith
  linarith

/-- **The symmetry barrier is exactly half the orbit oscillation (lower bound).**  On the orbit
of a single sequence, no invariant model beats half the spread of the target. -/
theorem orbit_barrier_lower [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (g : Seq ι κ → ℝ) (x : Seq ι κ)
    {p : Seq ι κ → ℝ} (hp : Invariant p) :
    ((Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty fun σ : Equiv.Perm ι => g (permAct σ x))
        - Finset.univ.inf' Finset.univ_nonempty fun σ : Equiv.Perm ι => g (permAct σ x)) / 2
      ≤ Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty
          fun σ : Equiv.Perm ι => |p (permAct σ x) - g (permAct σ x)| := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨sM, -, hsM⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_sup' (Finset.univ_nonempty (α := Equiv.Perm ι))
    (fun σ : Equiv.Perm ι => g (permAct σ x))
  obtain ⟨sm, -, hsm⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_inf' (Finset.univ_nonempty (α := Equiv.Perm ι))
    (fun σ : Equiv.Perm ι => g (permAct σ x))
  have hM : |p (permAct sM x) - g (permAct sM x)|
      ≤ Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty
          fun σ : Equiv.Perm ι => |p (permAct σ x) - g (permAct σ x)| :=
    Finset.le_sup' (fun σ : Equiv.Perm ι => |p (permAct σ x) - g (permAct σ x)|)
      (Finset.mem_univ sM)
  have hm : |p (permAct sm x) - g (permAct sm x)|
      ≤ Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty
          fun σ : Equiv.Perm ι => |p (permAct σ x) - g (permAct σ x)| :=
    Finset.le_sup' (fun σ : Equiv.Perm ι => |p (permAct σ x) - g (permAct σ x)|)
      (Finset.mem_univ sm)
  have e1 : p (permAct sM x) = p x := hp sM x
  have e2 : p (permAct sm x) = p x := hp sm x
  have hconst : p (permAct sM x) = p (permAct sm x) := by rw [e1, e2]
  have h1 : g (permAct sM x) - p (permAct sM x) ≤ |p (permAct sM x) - g (permAct sM x)| := by
    rw [abs_sub_comm]; exact le_abs_self _
  have h2 : p (permAct sm x) - g (permAct sm x) ≤ |p (permAct sm x) - g (permAct sm x)| :=
    le_abs_self _
  rw [hsM, hsm]
  linarith

/-- **The bound is attained**: the constant midpoint model is invariant and achieves exactly
half the orbit oscillation, so `orbit_barrier_lower` is sharp. -/
theorem orbit_barrier_attained [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (g : Seq ι κ → ℝ) (x : Seq ι κ) :
    ∃ p : Seq ι κ → ℝ, Invariant p ∧ ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm ι,
      |p (permAct σ x) - g (permAct σ x)|
        ≤ ((Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty fun τ : Equiv.Perm ι => g (permAct τ x))
            - Finset.univ.inf' Finset.univ_nonempty
                fun τ : Equiv.Perm ι => g (permAct τ x)) / 2 := by
  classical
  set M := Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty fun τ : Equiv.Perm ι => g (permAct τ x) with hMdef
  set m := Finset.univ.inf' Finset.univ_nonempty fun τ : Equiv.Perm ι => g (permAct τ x) with hmdef
  refine ⟨fun _ => (M + m) / 2, fun _ _ => rfl, ?_⟩
  intro σ
  have hle : g (permAct σ x) ≤ M := by
    rw [hMdef]
    exact Finset.le_sup' (fun τ : Equiv.Perm ι => g (permAct τ x)) (Finset.mem_univ σ)
  have hge : m ≤ g (permAct σ x) := by
    rw [hmdef]
    exact Finset.inf'_le (fun τ : Equiv.Perm ι => g (permAct τ x)) (Finset.mem_univ σ)
  rw [abs_le]
  constructor <;> linarith

/-- **The symmetry barrier for position reading.**  If a token symmetry `σ` moves position `i₀`,
then no `σ`-invariant model reads position `i₀` to uniform accuracy better than `1/2`.  This
applies verbatim to fully permutation-symmetric models and to shift-symmetric (relative
positional encoding) models. -/
theorem symmetry_barrier_position_read [DecidableEq ι] [DecidableEq κ] {σ : Equiv.Perm ι}
    {i₀ : ι} (hne : σ i₀ ≠ i₀) (a₀ : κ) (p : Seq ι κ → ℝ)
    (hp : ∀ x, p (permAct σ x) = p x) :
    ∃ x : Seq ι κ, (1:ℝ)/2 ≤ |p x - x i₀ a₀| := by
  classical
  set u : Seq ι κ := fun i a => if i = i₀ ∧ a = a₀ then (1:ℝ) else 0 with hu
  have hu0 : u i₀ a₀ = 1 := by simp [hu]
  have hv0 : (permAct σ u) i₀ a₀ = 0 := by
    show u (σ i₀) a₀ = 0
    simp [hu, hne]
  have hdefect := invariant_defect_lower_bound (g := fun y : Seq ι κ => y i₀ a₀) hp u
  simp only [hu0, hv0] at hdefect
  by_cases h : (1:ℝ)/2 ≤ |p u - u i₀ a₀|
  · exact ⟨u, h⟩
  · refine ⟨permAct σ u, ?_⟩
    push_neg at h
    rw [hu0] at h
    rw [hv0]
    have habs : |(1:ℝ) - 0| = 1 := by norm_num
    rw [habs] at hdefect
    linarith

/-- **A concrete symmetry barrier.**  Reading the first token of a two-token sequence is beyond
every permutation-invariant model: the uniform error is at least `1/2`.  Smallest instance of
`symmetry_barrier_position_read`. -/
theorem no_symmetric_model_reads_first_token
    (p : Seq (Fin 2) (Fin 1) → ℝ) (hp : Invariant p) :
    ∃ x : Seq (Fin 2) (Fin 1), (1:ℝ)/2 ≤ |p x - x 0 0| :=
  symmetry_barrier_position_read (σ := Equiv.swap 0 1) (i₀ := 0) (by decide) 0 p
    (fun x => hp (Equiv.swap 0 1) x)

end NegativeHalf

section PositionalRepair

variable {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ]

/-- One-hot positional encoding: each token keeps its features and acquires an extra block of
`ι` coordinates holding the indicator of its own position. -/
def posEnc (x : Seq ι κ) : Seq ι (κ ⊕ ι) :=
  fun i => Sum.elim (x i) (fun j => if j = i then (1:ℝ) else 0)

omit [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] in
theorem continuous_posEnc : Continuous (posEnc (ι := ι) (κ := κ)) := by
  apply continuous_pi
  intro i
  apply continuous_pi
  intro c
  cases c with
  | inl a => exact (continuous_apply a).comp (continuous_apply i)
  | inr j => exact continuous_const

/-- Positionally tagged sequences can be decoded *invariantly*: attending from the tag block to
the feature block reconstructs the ordered sequence, and the reconstruction is a sum over
tokens, hence permutation invariant. -/
def decodeSeq (z : Seq ι (κ ⊕ ι)) : Seq ι κ :=
  fun i a => ∑ j, z j (Sum.inr i) * z j (Sum.inl a)

omit [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ] in
theorem continuous_decodeSeq : Continuous (decodeSeq (ι := ι) (κ := κ)) := by
  apply continuous_pi
  intro i
  apply continuous_pi
  intro a
  apply continuous_finset_sum
  intro j _
  have h1 : Continuous fun z : Seq ι (κ ⊕ ι) => z j (Sum.inr i) :=
    (continuous_apply (Sum.inr i)).comp (continuous_apply j)
  have h2 : Continuous fun z : Seq ι (κ ⊕ ι) => z j (Sum.inl a) :=
    (continuous_apply (Sum.inl a)).comp (continuous_apply j)
  exact h1.mul h2

omit [Fintype κ] in
/-- **The decoder inverts the positional encoding.** -/
theorem decodeSeq_posEnc (x : Seq ι κ) : decodeSeq (posEnc x) = x := by
  funext i a
  show ∑ j, (if i = j then (1:ℝ) else 0) * x j a = x i a
  rw [Finset.sum_eq_single i]
  · simp
  · intro j _ hj
    simp [Ne.symm hj]
  · intro h; exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ i) h

omit [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ] in
/-- **The decoder is permutation invariant**, so any functional built through it is invariant. -/
theorem decodeSeq_invariant (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) (z : Seq ι (κ ⊕ ι)) :
    decodeSeq (permAct σ z) = decodeSeq z := by
  funext i a
  show ∑ j, z (σ j) (Sum.inr i) * z (σ j) (Sum.inl a)
      = ∑ j, z j (Sum.inr i) * z j (Sum.inl a)
  exact Equiv.sum_comp σ (fun j => z j (Sum.inr i) * z j (Sum.inl a))

/-- The saturation of the positionally encoded image of a set. -/
def encSaturation (K : Set (Seq ι κ)) : Set (Seq ι (κ ⊕ ι)) :=
  ⋃ σ : Equiv.Perm ι, (permAct σ) '' (posEnc '' K)

omit [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] in
theorem posEnc_mem_encSaturation {K : Set (Seq ι κ)} {x : Seq ι κ} (hx : x ∈ K) :
    posEnc x ∈ encSaturation K :=
  Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨1, ⟨posEnc x, ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩, rfl⟩⟩

omit [Fintype κ] in
theorem isCompact_encSaturation {K : Set (Seq ι κ)} (hK : IsCompact K) :
    IsCompact (encSaturation K) :=
  isCompact_iUnion fun σ =>
    ((hK.image continuous_posEnc).image (continuous_permAct σ))

omit [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] in
theorem saturated_encSaturation (K : Set (Seq ι κ)) : Saturated (encSaturation K) := by
  rintro tau z hz
  rw [encSaturation, Set.mem_iUnion] at hz ⊢
  obtain ⟨σ, w, hw, rfl⟩ := hz
  exact ⟨σ * tau, w, hw, (permAct_comp tau σ w).symm ▸ rfl⟩

/-- **Positional encodings restore full universality.**  With the one-hot positional encoding,
*permutation-invariant* models on the augmented feature space `κ ⊕ ι` approximate every
continuous sequence functional uniformly on every compact set — including all the
order-sensitive functionals ruled out by `symmetry_barrier_position_read`. -/
theorem positional_restores_universality (g : C(Seq ι κ, ℝ)) {K : Set (Seq ι κ)}
    (hK : IsCompact K) {eps : ℝ} (heps : 0 < eps) :
    ∃ p ∈ attentionAlgebra ι (κ ⊕ ι),
      Invariant (fun z => p z) ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, |p (posEnc x) - g x| < eps := by
  set G : C(Seq ι (κ ⊕ ι), ℝ) := g.comp ⟨decodeSeq, continuous_decodeSeq⟩ with hG
  have hGinv : Invariant (fun z => G z) := by
    intro σ z
    show g (decodeSeq (permAct σ z)) = g (decodeSeq z)
    rw [decodeSeq_invariant]
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpinv, hclose⟩ :=
    symmetric_uniform_universal (ι := ι) (κ := κ ⊕ ι) G hGinv
      (isCompact_encSaturation hK) (saturated_encSaturation K) heps
  refine ⟨p, hp, hpinv, ?_⟩
  intro x hx
  have := hclose (posEnc x) (posEnc_mem_encSaturation hx)
  have hGx : G (posEnc x) = g x := by
    show g (decodeSeq (posEnc x)) = g x
    rw [decodeSeq_posEnc]
  rwa [hGx] at this

/-- **Sequence-to-sequence universality with positional encoding.**  Every continuous map from
sequences to sequences is approximated, uniformly on compacta and simultaneously in all output
positions and features, by permutation-invariant attention models applied to the positionally
encoded input. -/
theorem positional_seq2seq_universality (F : Seq ι κ → Seq ι κ)
    (hF : ∀ i a, Continuous fun x => F x i a) {K : Set (Seq ι κ)} (hK : IsCompact K)
    {eps : ℝ} (heps : 0 < eps) :
    ∃ P : ι → κ → C(Seq ι (κ ⊕ ι), ℝ),
      (∀ i a, P i a ∈ attentionAlgebra ι (κ ⊕ ι)) ∧
      (∀ i a, Invariant (fun z => P i a z)) ∧
      ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ i a, |P i a (posEnc x) - F x i a| < eps := by
  choose P hP hPinv hclose using fun (i : ι) (a : κ) =>
    positional_restores_universality (ι := ι) (κ := κ) ⟨fun x => F x i a, hF i a⟩ hK heps
  exact ⟨P, hP, hPinv, fun x hx i a => hclose i a x hx⟩

end PositionalRepair

section EquivariantHeads

variable {ι κ : Type*} [DecidableEq ι]

/-- The marked-query encoding: the queried position `i` is flagged by an extra feature. -/
def markAt (i : ι) (x : Seq ι κ) : Seq ι (κ ⊕ Unit) :=
  fun j => Sum.elim (x j) (fun _ => if j = i then (1:ℝ) else 0)

theorem markAt_permAct (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) (i : ι) (x : Seq ι κ) :
    markAt i (permAct σ x) = permAct σ (markAt (σ i) x) := by
  funext j c
  cases c with
  | inl a => rfl
  | inr _ =>
      show (if j = i then (1:ℝ) else 0) = if σ j = σ i then (1:ℝ) else 0
      by_cases h : j = i
      · simp [h]
      · simp [h]

/-- **Marked invariant functionals are exactly equivariant heads.**  If `G` is invariant under a
token symmetry `σ`, then the head `i ↦ G (markAt i x)` is `σ`-equivariant: permuting the input
tokens permutes the outputs, which is the symmetry a positional-encoding-free transformer layer
possesses. -/
theorem marked_head_equivariant {G : Seq ι (κ ⊕ Unit) → ℝ} {σ : Equiv.Perm ι}
    (hG : ∀ z, G (permAct σ z) = G z) (i : ι) (x : Seq ι κ) :
    G (markAt i (permAct σ x)) = G (markAt (σ i) x) := by
  rw [markAt_permAct, hG]

end EquivariantHeads

section EquivariantUniversality

variable {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ]
variable {Γ : Type*} [Group Γ] [Fintype Γ]

/-- The feature block of an augmented (marked) sequence. -/
def feat (z : Seq ι (κ ⊕ Unit)) : Seq ι κ := fun i a => z i (Sum.inl a)

/-- The mark coordinate of an augmented sequence. -/
def markCoord (z : Seq ι (κ ⊕ Unit)) (i : ι) : ℝ := z i (Sum.inr ())

/-- A sequence-to-sequence map is *`Γ`-equivariant* when a token symmetry of the input permutes
the output tokens the same way. -/
def EquivariantUnder (act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι) (F : Seq ι κ → Seq ι κ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : Γ) (x : Seq ι κ) (i : ι) (a : κ), F (permAct (act g) x) i a = F x (act g i) a

/-- The *marked functional* of an equivariant map: contract the output of `F` on the feature
block against the mark coordinates.  This is the key construction: it converts an equivariant
sequence-to-sequence map into a genuinely **invariant** scalar functional of the marked
sequence, with no loss of information. -/
def markedFunctional (F : Seq ι κ → Seq ι κ) (a : κ) (z : Seq ι (κ ⊕ Unit)) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, F (feat z) i a * markCoord z i

omit [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ] in
theorem feat_permAct (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) (z : Seq ι (κ ⊕ Unit)) :
    feat (permAct σ z) = permAct σ (feat z) := rfl

omit [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ] [Fintype Γ] in
/-- **Equivariance becomes invariance after marking.** -/
theorem markedFunctional_invariant {act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι} {F : Seq ι κ → Seq ι κ}
    (hF : EquivariantUnder act F) (a : κ) :
    InvariantUnder act (markedFunctional F a) := by
  intro gamma z
  show ∑ i, F (feat (permAct (act gamma) z)) i a * markCoord (permAct (act gamma) z) i
      = ∑ i, F (feat z) i a * markCoord z i
  rw [feat_permAct]
  have hstep : ∀ i : ι, F (permAct (act gamma) (feat z)) i a * markCoord (permAct (act gamma) z) i
      = F (feat z) (act gamma i) a * markCoord z (act gamma i) := by
    intro i
    rw [hF gamma (feat z) i a]
    rfl
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => hstep i)]
  exact Equiv.sum_comp (act gamma) (fun i => F (feat z) i a * markCoord z i)

omit [Fintype κ] in
/-- The marked functional reproduces `F` exactly on marked sequences. -/
theorem markedFunctional_markAt (F : Seq ι κ → Seq ι κ) (a : κ) (i : ι) (x : Seq ι κ) :
    markedFunctional F a (markAt i x) = F x i a := by
  have hfeat : feat (markAt i x) = x := rfl
  show ∑ i', F (feat (markAt i x)) i' a * markCoord (markAt i x) i' = F x i a
  rw [hfeat]
  have hmark : ∀ i' : ι, markCoord (markAt i x) i' = if i' = i then (1:ℝ) else 0 := fun _ => rfl
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i' _ => by rw [hmark i'])]
  rw [Finset.sum_eq_single i]
  · simp
  · intro i' _ hi'; simp [hi']
  · intro h; exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ i) h

omit [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ] in
theorem continuous_markedFunctional {F : Seq ι κ → Seq ι κ}
    (hF : ∀ i a, Continuous fun x => F x i a) (a : κ) :
    Continuous (markedFunctional F a) := by
  apply continuous_finset_sum
  intro i _
  have hfeat : Continuous (feat (ι := ι) (κ := κ)) := by
    apply continuous_pi; intro m; apply continuous_pi; intro b
    exact (continuous_apply (Sum.inl b)).comp (continuous_apply m)
  have h1 : Continuous fun z : Seq ι (κ ⊕ Unit) => F (feat z) i a := (hF i a).comp hfeat
  have h2 : Continuous fun z : Seq ι (κ ⊕ Unit) => markCoord z i :=
    (continuous_apply (Sum.inr ())).comp (continuous_apply i)
  exact h1.mul h2

omit [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] in
theorem continuous_markAt (i : ι) : Continuous (markAt (κ := κ) i) := by
  apply continuous_pi; intro j; apply continuous_pi; intro c
  cases c with
  | inl a => exact (continuous_apply a).comp (continuous_apply j)
  | inr _ => exact continuous_const

/-- The symmetry saturation of the marked image of a set of sequences. -/
def markSaturation (act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι) (K : Set (Seq ι κ)) : Set (Seq ι (κ ⊕ Unit)) :=
  ⋃ g : Γ, ⋃ i : ι, (permAct (act g)) '' (markAt i '' K)

omit [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] [Fintype Γ] in
theorem markAt_mem_markSaturation (act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι) {K : Set (Seq ι κ)} {x : Seq ι κ}
    (hx : x ∈ K) (i : ι) : markAt i x ∈ markSaturation act K :=
  Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨1, Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨i, ⟨markAt i x, ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩, by simp⟩⟩⟩

omit [Fintype κ] in
theorem isCompact_markSaturation (act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι) {K : Set (Seq ι κ)}
    (hK : IsCompact K) : IsCompact (markSaturation act K) :=
  isCompact_iUnion fun g =>
    isCompact_iUnion fun i => ((hK.image (continuous_markAt i)).image (continuous_permAct (act g)))

omit [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] [Fintype Γ] in
theorem saturated_markSaturation (act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι) (K : Set (Seq ι κ)) :
    SaturatedUnder act (markSaturation act K) := by
  rintro tau z hz
  rw [markSaturation, Set.mem_iUnion] at hz ⊢
  obtain ⟨gamma, hz⟩ := hz
  rw [Set.mem_iUnion] at hz
  obtain ⟨i, w, hw, rfl⟩ := hz
  refine ⟨gamma * tau, ?_⟩
  rw [Set.mem_iUnion]
  refine ⟨i, w, hw, ?_⟩
  rw [MonoidHom.map_mul]
  exact (permAct_comp (act tau) (act gamma) w).symm ▸ rfl

/-- **Equivariant universality: the exact converse of the symmetry barrier.**
A `Γ`-invariant attention model, queried through the marked encoding, uniformly approximates
*every* continuous `Γ`-equivariant sequence-to-sequence map on every compact domain — and the
resulting head family is itself exactly `Γ`-equivariant.

Together with `symmetry_barrier_position_read` (no invariant model can approximate a
non-equivariant target) and `positional_restores_universality` (positional encodings remove the
restriction), this pins down the expressive power of symmetric attention: it is precisely the
equivariant continuous maps. -/
theorem equivariant_uniform_universal (act : Γ →* Equiv.Perm ι) (F : Seq ι κ → Seq ι κ)
    (hFc : ∀ i a, Continuous fun x => F x i a) (hFe : EquivariantUnder act F)
    {K : Set (Seq ι κ)} (hK : IsCompact K) {eps : ℝ} (heps : 0 < eps) :
    ∃ P : κ → C(Seq ι (κ ⊕ Unit), ℝ),
      (∀ a, P a ∈ attentionAlgebra ι (κ ⊕ Unit)) ∧
      (∀ a, InvariantUnder act (fun z => P a z)) ∧
      (∀ (a : κ) (g : Γ) (i : ι) (x : Seq ι κ),
        P a (markAt i (permAct (act g) x)) = P a (markAt (act g i) x)) ∧

Numerical demonstrations of the symmetry dichotomy for attention architectures.

the algebra of real polynomials in readouts: sums model multi-head attention,
products model the multiplicative interaction generated by stacking layers.

  D1  Uniform-score softmax heads ARE readouts.
  D2  Position-reading barrier: any permutation-invariant model errs by >= 1/2

  D3  Orbit barrier equality: the optimal invariant error on an orbit is

  D4  Averaging is free: symmetrizing an approximant of an invariant target

  D5  Symmetric universality: invariant elements of the attention algebra

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
from typing import Callable, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

import numpy as np

Array = np.ndarray
Perm = Tuple[int, ...]


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Core objects: the token action, readouts, softmax heads
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def act(sigma: Perm, x: Array) -> Array:
    """Token action: (sigma . x)[i] = x[sigma(i)].  x has shape (n, d)."""
    return x[list(sigma), :]


def all_perms(n: int) -> List[Perm]:
    """The full symmetric group on {0, ..., n-1}."""
    return list(itertools.permutations(range(n)))


def cyclic_group(n: int) -> List[Perm]:
    """The cyclic shift group generated by i -> i+1 mod n."""
    return [tuple((i + k) % n for i in range(n)) for k in range(n)]


def readout(w: Array, x: Array) -> float:
    """R_w(x) = sum_i sum_a w[i,a] x[i,a]."""
    return float(np.sum(w * x))


def softmax_head(scores: Array, w: Array, x: Array) -> float:
    """A genuine softmax attention head: softmax(scores) . (row-wise w-values)."""
    e = np.exp(scores - np.max(scores))
    alpha = e / np.sum(e)
    values = np.sum(w * x, axis=1)
    return float(np.dot(alpha, values))


def demo_1_heads_are_readouts() -> None:
    print("D1  Uniform-score softmax heads are exactly readouts")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    n, d = 4, 3
    w = rng.normal(size=(n, d))
    x = rng.normal(size=(n, d))
    lhs = softmax_head(np.zeros(n), w, x)
    rhs = readout(w / n, x)
    print(f"    softmax head with zero scores : {lhs: .10f}")
    print(f"    readout with weights w/n      : {rhs: .10f}")
    print(f"    agree to 1e-12                : {abs(lhs - rhs) < 1e-12}")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# D2 / D3: the sharp barrier
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def orbit(group: Sequence[Perm], x: Array) -> List[Array]:
    return [act(s, x) for s in group]


def orbit_barrier(target: Callable[[Array], float],
                  x: Array,
                  group: Sequence[Perm]) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """Return (optimal invariant error on the orbit of x, optimal model value).

    Theory: an invariant model is constant on the orbit, so the best it can do
    is the midpoint of the range of the target over the orbit, and the error is
    exactly half the oscillation.
    """
    vals = [target(y) for y in orbit(group, x)]
    hi, lo = max(vals), min(vals)
    return (hi - lo) / 2.0, (hi + lo) / 2.0


def demo_2_position_barrier() -> None:
    print("D2  Position-reading barrier: reading token 0 costs at least 1/2")

        pts[:, 0] + pts[:, 1],
        pts[:, 0] * pts[:, 1],

def demo_3_orbit_equality() -> None:

        attained = max(abs(best - v) for v in vals)
        # Lower bound: no invariant model (i.e. no constant on the orbit) beats it.
        sweep = min(max(abs(c - v) for v in vals)
                    for c in np.linspace(min(vals) - 1, max(vals) + 1, 20001))
        print(f"    trial {trial}: osc/2 = {osc / 2:.6f} | midpoint attains "
              f"{attained:.6f} | best over all constants {sweep:.6f}")
    print("    -> lower bound and achievability coincide.")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# D4 / D5: the positive half
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def monomial_exponents(n_feats: int, degree: int) -> List[Tuple[int, ...]]:
    """All exponent vectors of total degree <= `degree` over `n_feats` readouts."""
    out: List[Tuple[int, ...]] = []
    for total in range(degree + 1):
        for combo in itertools.combinations_with_replacement(range(n_feats), total):
            e = [0] * n_feats
            for c in combo:
                e[c] += 1
            out.append(tuple(e))
    return out


def attention_features(x: Array, weights: Sequence[Array],
                       exps: Sequence[Tuple[int, ...]]) -> Array:
    """Evaluate the monomials in the readouts R_{w_1}, ..., R_{w_m} at x.

    Each returned coordinate is an element of the attention algebra.
    """
    base = np.array([readout(w, x) for w in weights])
    return np.array([float(np.prod(base ** np.array(e))) for e in exps])


def symmetrize(model: Callable[[Array], float],
               group: Sequence[Perm]) -> Callable[[Array], float]:
    """Group averaging: S_G f (x) = (1/|G|) sum_g f(g . x)."""
    def averaged(x: Array) -> float:
        return float(np.mean([model(act(s, x)) for s in group]))
    return averaged


def demo_4_averaging_is_free() -> None:
    print("D4  Averaging is free: symmetrizing never hurts on an invariant target")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
    n, d = 3, 2
    group = all_perms(n)
    # An invariant target: a symmetric function of the tokens.
    target = lambda y: float(np.sum(np.sum(y, axis=1) ** 2))

    weights = [rng.normal(size=(n, d)) for _ in range(4)]
    exps = monomial_exponents(len(weights), degree=2)

    # A deliberately ASYMMETRIC fit: train only on unsaturated samples.
    train = [rng.normal(size=(n, d)) for _ in range(400)]
    A = np.stack([attention_features(x, weights, exps) for x in train])
    b = np.array([target(x) for x in train])
    coef, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, b, rcond=None)
    raw = lambda x: float(np.dot(coef, attention_features(x, weights, exps)))
    sym = symmetrize(raw, group)

    test = [rng.normal(size=(n, d)) for _ in range(300)]
    saturated = [act(s, x) for x in test for s in group]
    e_raw = max(abs(raw(x) - target(x)) for x in saturated)
    e_sym = max(abs(sym(x) - target(x)) for x in saturated)
    print(f"    sup error, unsymmetrized model : {e_raw:.6f}")
    print(f"    sup error, symmetrized model   : {e_sym:.6f}")
    print(f"    symmetrization did not hurt    : {e_sym <= e_raw + 1e-9}")
    print(f"    symmetrized model is invariant : "
          f"{max(abs(sym(act(s, test[0])) - sym(test[0])) for s in group) < 1e-9}")
    print()


def demo_5_symmetric_universality() -> None:
    print("D5  Symmetric universality: error shrinks as the algebra degree grows")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(11)
    n, d = 3, 2
    group = all_perms(n)
    # Invariant, genuinely nonlinear target: a multisymmetric power sum mixture.
    def target(y: Array) -> float:
        return float(np.sum(y[:, 0] ** 2 * y[:, 1]) + np.sum(np.tanh(y[:, 1])))

    # Coordinate readouts span all linear functionals; symmetrized monomials in
    # them span the invariant part of the attention algebra degree by degree.
    weights: List[Array] = []
    for i in range(n):
        for a in range(d):
            w = np.zeros((n, d))
            w[i, a] = 1.0
            weights.append(w)

    train = [rng.normal(scale=0.5, size=(n, d)) for _ in range(2000)]
    test = [rng.normal(scale=0.5, size=(n, d)) for _ in range(300)]

    for degree in (1, 2, 3, 4, 5):
        exps = monomial_exponents(len(weights), degree)
        def feats(x: Array, exps: Sequence[Tuple[int, ...]] = exps) -> Array:
            # symmetrized features: average the monomials over the group
            return np.mean([attention_features(act(s, x), weights, exps)
                            for s in group], axis=0)
        A = np.stack([feats(x) for x in train])
        b = np.array([target(x) for x in train])
        # Column rescaling keeps the (badly conditioned) monomial basis usable.
        scale = np.maximum(np.sqrt(np.mean(A ** 2, axis=0)), 1e-12)
        coef, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A / scale, b, rcond=1e-10)
        errs = [abs(float(np.dot(coef, feats(x) / scale)) - target(x))
                for x in test]
        rms = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(np.square(errs))))
        print(f"    degree {degree}: #invariant features = {len(exps):4d} | "
              f"sup error = {max(errs):.6f} | rms error = {rms:.6f}")
    print("    -> density of the invariant part of the attention algebra.")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# D6: positional encoding and the invariant decoder
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def pos_encode(x: Array) -> Array:
    """One-hot positional encoding: append the indicator of the token's index."""
    n, _ = x.shape
    return np.concatenate([x, np.eye(n)], axis=1)


def invariant_decode(z: Array, n_feats: int) -> Array:
    """dec(z)[i,a] = sum_j z[j, pos(i)] * z[j, feat(a)] -- one attention pattern.

    This is a sum over tokens, hence permutation-invariant, yet it inverts the
    one-hot positional encoding exactly.
    """
    feats = z[:, :n_feats]
    tags = z[:, n_feats:]
    return tags.T @ feats


def demo_6_positional_repair() -> None:
    print("D6  Positional repair: an invariant quadratic decoder inverts the encoding")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(5)
    n, d = 4, 3
    x = rng.normal(size=(n, d))
    z = pos_encode(x)
    print(f"    ||dec(enc(x)) - x||_inf                    : "
          f"{np.max(np.abs(invariant_decode(z, d) - x)):.2e}")
    worst = 0.0
    for s in all_perms(n):
        worst = max(worst, float(np.max(np.abs(
            invariant_decode(act(s, z), d) - invariant_decode(z, d)))))
    print(f"    max change of dec under all n! permutations: {worst:.2e}")
    print("    -> the decoder is exactly permutation-invariant AND inverts enc,")
    print("       so invariant models on encoded input read absolute positions.")

    # Concretely: an invariant model on encoded input recovers x[0,0] exactly,
    # which by D2 is impossible without the encoding.
    read_first = lambda zz: float(invariant_decode(zz, d)[0, 0])
    errs = [abs(read_first(act(s, z)) - x[0, 0]) for s in all_perms(n)]
    print(f"    invariant read of x[0,0] on encoded input, max error over the")
    print(f"    whole orbit: {max(errs):.2e}   (barrier without encoding: 0.5)")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# D7: equivariance = marked invariance
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def mark_at(i: int, x: Array) -> Array:
    """Marked-token encoding: append a single feature flagging position i."""
    n, _ = x.shape
    flag = np.zeros((n, 1))
    flag[i, 0] = 1.0
    return np.concatenate([x, flag], axis=1)


def marked_functional(F: Callable[[Array], Array], a: int, z: Array) -> float:
    """G_a(z) = sum_i F(feat(z))[i,a] * mark(z)[i]."""
    feats = z[:, :-1]
    mark = z[:, -1]
    return float(np.dot(F(feats)[:, a], mark))


def demo_7_equivariance_is_marked_invariance() -> None:
    print("D7  Equivariance = invariance, seen through the marked-token window")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(13)
    n, d = 3, 2
    group = all_perms(n)

    # A permutation-equivariant sequence-to-sequence map: each token's output
    # depends on its own features and on order-free statistics of the whole set.
    def F(x: Array) -> Array:
        pooled = np.sum(x, axis=0, keepdims=True)
        return np.tanh(x) + 0.3 * x * pooled

    x = rng.normal(size=(n, d))

    # (a) F really is equivariant.
    eq = max(float(np.max(np.abs(F(act(s, x)) - act(s, F(x))))) for s in group)
    print(f"    equivariance defect of F                : {eq:.2e}")

    # (b) The marked functional is invariant ...
    z = mark_at(1, x)
    inv = max(abs(marked_functional(F, 0, act(s, z)) - marked_functional(F, 0, z))
              for s in group)
    print(f"    invariance defect of the marked functional: {inv:.2e}")

    # (c) ... and reproduces F exactly on marked sequences.
    rep = max(abs(marked_functional(F, a, mark_at(i, x)) - F(x)[i, a])
              for i in range(n) for a in range(d))
    print(f"    ||G_a(mark_i(x)) - F(x)[i,a]||_inf        : {rep:.2e}")

    # (d) The induced head family is EXACTLY equivariant, not approximately.
    head_defect = max(
        abs(marked_functional(F, a, mark_at(i, act(s, x)))
            - marked_functional(F, a, mark_at(s[i], x)))
        for s in group for i in range(n) for a in range(d))
    print(f"    exact equivariance of the head family     : {head_defect:.2e}")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bonus: the cyclic (relative-encoding) regime inherits the same barrier
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_8_relative_encoding_barrier() -> None:
    print("D8  Relative (cyclic) symmetry inherits the 1/2 absolute-position barrier")
    n, d = 5, 1
    group = cyclic_group(n)
    u = np.zeros((n, d))
    u[0, 0] = 1.0
    target = lambda y: float(y[0, 0])
    err, best = orbit_barrier(target, u, group)
    print(f"    cyclic orbit values of 'read token 0' : "
          f"{[float(t[0, 0]) for t in orbit(group, u)]}")
    print(f"    optimal shift-invariant error         : {err:.4f}  (theory: 0.5)")

    # But a SHIFT-INVARIANT target is approximated perfectly by a shift-invariant

any model invariant under that group, restricted to the orbit of x:

        optimal value  =  (max_orbit g  +  min_orbit g) / 2,

from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple

Seq = Tuple[Tuple[float, ...], ...]      # n tokens x d features
Perm = Tuple[int, ...]

    """Token action: (sigma . x)[i] = x[sigma(i)]."""
    return tuple(x[sigma[i]] for i in range(len(x)))


def symmetric_group(n: int) -> List[Perm]:
    return list(itertools.permutations(range(n)))


def cyclic_group(n: int) -> List[Perm]:
    return [tuple((i + k) % n for i in range(n)) for k in range(n)]


def orbit_certificate(target: Callable[[Seq], float],
                      x: Seq,
                      group: Sequence[Perm]) -> Dict[str, object]:
    """Exact optimal invariant error on the orbit of x, with witnesses."""
    pairs = [(target(act(s, x)), s) for s in group]
    hi_val, hi_perm = max(pairs, key=lambda p: p[0])
    lo_val, lo_perm = min(pairs, key=lambda p: p[0])
    return {
        "oscillation": hi_val - lo_val,
        "optimal_error": (hi_val - lo_val) / 2.0,
        "optimal_value": (hi_val + lo_val) / 2.0,
        "argmax_permutation": hi_perm,
        "argmin_permutation": lo_perm,
        "max_value": hi_val,
        "min_value": lo_val,
        "orbit_size": len(set(act(s, x) for s in group)),
    }


def verify_by_sweep(target: Callable[[Seq], float],
                    x: Seq,
                    group: Sequence[Perm],
                    steps: int = 100001) -> float:
    """Brute-force minimum over all constant (hence invariant) models."""
    vals = [target(act(s, x)) for s in group]
    lo, hi = min(vals) - 1.0, max(vals) + 1.0
    best = float("inf")
    for k in range(steps):
        c = lo + (hi - lo) * k / (steps - 1)
        best = min(best, max(abs(c - v) for v in vals))
    return best

           x: Seq,
           group: Sequence[Perm]) -> None:

    sweep = verify_by_sweep(target, x, group)

    print(f"    orbit size                  : {cert['orbit_size']}")
    print(f"    max over orbit              : {cert['max_value']:.6f} "

                     group: Sequence[Perm]) -> Callable[[np.ndarray], float]:
    """Return the group average (1/|G|) sum_g model(g . x).

    The averaged model is exactly invariant under the group, stays inside the
    attention algebra (because precomposing a readout with a permutation only
    permutes its weight table), and -- on a target that is itself invariant over
    a domain closed under the group -- has uniform error no larger than the
    original model's.
    """
    members = list(group)
    scale = 1.0 / len(members)

    def averaged(x: np.ndarray) -> float:
        return scale * sum(model(act(s, x)) for s in members)

    return averaged

    """Closed form for the linear case: averaging a readout averages its rows.

    Costs no extra forward evaluations at inference time, unlike the generic
    procedure, which pays |G| evaluations per call.
    """
    return np.mean([w[list(s), :] for s in group], axis=0)


def uniform_error(model: Callable[[np.ndarray], float],
                  target: Callable[[np.ndarray], float],
                  samples: Sequence[np.ndarray],
                  group: Sequence[Perm]) -> float:
    """Worst error over the group-saturation of a finite sample set."""
    return max(abs(model(act(s, x)) - target(act(s, x)))
               for x in samples for s in group)

    n, d = 3, 2

    samples = [rng.normal(size=(n, d)) for _ in range(200)]

    "positional_repair_algorithm": "from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
from typing import Callable, List, Sequence, Tuple

import numpy as np

Perm = Tuple[int, ...]


def act(sigma: Perm, x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    return x[list(sigma), :]


def pos_encode(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """One-hot positional encoding: append the indicator of the token's index."""
    n = x.shape[0]
    return np.concatenate([x, np.eye(n)], axis=1)


def invariant_decode(z: np.ndarray, n_feats: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """dec(z)[i,a] = sum_j z[j, pos(i)] * z[j, feat(a)].

    One attention pattern: the tag block supplies the weights, the feature block
    supplies the values.  It is a sum over tokens, hence exactly permutation
    invariant, and it inverts pos_encode exactly.
    """
    return z[:, n_feats:].T @ z[:, :n_feats]


def monomial_exponents(m: int, degree: int) -> List[Tuple[int, ...]]:
    out: List[Tuple[int, ...]] = []
    for total in range(degree + 1):
        for combo in itertools.combinations_with_replacement(range(m), total):
            e = [0] * m
            for c in combo:
                e[c] += 1
            out.append(tuple(e))
    return out


def coordinate_readouts(n: int, d: int) -> List[np.ndarray]:
    ws: List[np.ndarray] = []
    for i in range(n):
        for a in range(d):
            w = np.zeros((n, d))
            w[i, a] = 1.0
            ws.append(w)
    return ws


def invariant_features(x: np.ndarray,
                       weights: Sequence[np.ndarray],
                       exps: Sequence[Tuple[int, ...]],
                       group: Sequence[Perm]) -> np.ndarray:
    """Group-averaged monomials in the readouts: a basis for the invariant part
    of the attention algebra up to the chosen degree."""
    rows = []
    for s in group:
        y = act(s, x)
        base = np.array([float(np.sum(w * y)) for w in weights])
        rows.append([float(np.prod(base ** np.array(e))) for e in exps])
    return np.mean(np.array(rows), axis=0)


def fit_invariant_model(target: Callable[[np.ndarray], float],
                        train: Sequence[np.ndarray],
                        weights: Sequence[np.ndarray],
                        degree: int,
                        group: Sequence[Perm]):
    """Least-squares fit of an invariant element of the attention algebra."""
    exps = monomial_exponents(len(weights), degree)
    A = np.stack([invariant_features(x, weights, exps, group) for x in train])
    b = np.array([target(x) for x in train])
    scale = np.maximum(np.sqrt(np.mean(A ** 2, axis=0)), 1e-12)
    coef, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A / scale, b, rcond=1e-10)

    def model(x: np.ndarray) -> float:
        return float(np.dot(coef, invariant_features(x, weights, exps, group) / scale))

    return model


def decode_and_approximate(target: Callable[[np.ndarray], float],
                           train: Sequence[np.ndarray],
                           n: int, d: int, degree: int,
                           group: Sequence[Perm]):
    """Fit a PERMUTATION-INVARIANT model that approximates an arbitrary (possibly
    order-sensitive) target, by first positionally encoding the input.

    The composite target g . dec is invariant on the augmented space, so the
    symmetric theory applies; and on genuinely encoded inputs g . dec equals g.
    """
    lifted = lambda z: target(invariant_decode(z, d))
    encoded = [pos_encode(x) for x in train]
    inner = fit_invariant_model(lifted, encoded,
                                coordinate_readouts(n, d + n), degree, group)
    return lambda x: inner(pos_encode(x))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
    n, d, degree = 3, 2, 2
    G = list(itertools.permutations(range(n)))
    train = [rng.normal(scale=0.5, size=(n, d)) for _ in range(400)]
    test = [rng.normal(scale=0.5, size=(n, d)) for _ in range(100)]
    target = lambda x: float(x[0, 0])            # blocked without encoding
    model = decode_and_approximate(target, train, n, d, degree, G)
    print("sup error of the invariant model on encoded input:",
          max(abs(model(x) - target(x)) for x in test),
          "  (barrier without encoding: 0.5)")

    n, d = 3, 2
    group = list(itertools.permutations(range(n)))
    degrees = [1, 2, 3, 4]

    train = [rng.normal(scale=0.5, size=(n, d)) for _ in range(1200)]
    test = [rng.normal(scale=0.5, size=(n, d)) for _ in range(200)]

    inv_target = (lambda y: float(np.sum(np.sum(y, axis=1) ** 2)
                                  + np.sum(np.tanh(y[:, 1]))))
    ord_target = lambda y: float(y[0, 0])

    w_raw = coordinate_readouts(n, d)
    e_inv = [fit_sup_error(inv_target, train, test, w_raw, k, group) for k in degrees]
    e_ord = [fit_sup_error(ord_target, train, test, w_raw, k, group) for k in degrees]

    # With positional encoding: same invariant model class, encoded inputs.
    w_enc = coordinate_readouts(n, d + n)
    train_e = [pos_encode(x) for x in train]
    test_e = [pos_encode(x) for x in test]
    tgt_e = lambda z: float(invariant_decode(z, d)[0, 0])   # = x[0,0] on encoded inputs
    e_rep = [fit_sup_error(tgt_e, train_e, test_e, w_enc, k, group) for k in [1, 2]]

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16.5, 4.8))

    ax = axes[0]
    ax.semilogy(degrees, np.maximum(e_inv, 1e-16), "o-", lw=2,
                label="invariant target (reachable)")
    ax.semilogy(degrees, np.maximum(e_ord, 1e-16), "s-", lw=2,
                label=r"order-sensitive target $x_{0,0}$ (blocked)")
    ax.axhline(0.5, color="crimson", ls="--", lw=1.5, label=r"barrier $1/2$")
    ax.set_xticks(degrees)
    ax.set_xlabel("degree of the invariant attention model")
    ax.set_ylabel("sup error on held-out sequences")
    ax.set_title("A. density inside, plateau outside")
    ax.legend(fontsize=9)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

    ax = axes[1]
    ax.semilogy([1, 2], np.maximum(e_rep, 1e-16), "d-", lw=2, color="seagreen",
                label="invariant model on positionally encoded input")
    ax.axhline(0.5, color="crimson", ls="--", lw=1.5, label=r"barrier without encoding")
    ax.set_xticks([1, 2])
    ax.set_xlabel("degree of the invariant attention model")
    ax.set_ylabel("sup error on held-out sequences")
    ax.set_title("B. one-hot tags remove the barrier\n(model stays fully symmetric)")
    ax.legend(fontsize=9)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

    ax = axes[2]
    x = rng.normal(size=(n, d))
    z = pos_encode(x)
    sigma = (2, 0, 1)
    panel = np.concatenate(
        [z, np.full((n, 1), np.nan), act(sigma, z)], axis=1)
    im = ax.imshow(panel, cmap="coolwarm", aspect="auto")
    ax.set_title("C. encoded sequence (left) and a permuted copy (right)\n"
                 f"invariant decoder output differs by "
                 f"{np.max(np.abs(invariant_decode(act(sigma, z), d) - invariant_decode(z, d))):.1e}")
    ax.set_xlabel("features: original block | position tags  ||  permuted copy")
    ax.set_ylabel("token")
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, fraction=0.046)

    fig.suptitle("Positional encoding as a repair, not as symmetry breaking",
                 fontsize=13, y=0.995)
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.92))
    fig.savefig("positional_repair.png", dpi=160)
    print("wrote positional_repair.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Future directions

1. **State the CSS dictionary with two classical codes precisely.**  The mission's
   expression `C₁/C₂` requires `C₂ ⊆ C₁`, while the usual CSS commutation condition
   is formulated using orthogonal complements.  A future development should give
   the exact equivalence between parity-check matrices, a length-two chain complex,
   and the resulting stabilizer group.

2. **Separate simplicial, cellular, and graph models.**  The present formalization
   proves the chain-complex dimension theorem over any field.  Realizing every
   binary CSS chain complex by a *simplicial complex with its standard incidence
   maps* is a substantially stronger representability claim and should not be
   conflated with merely viewing matrices as abstract differentials.  Determine
   necessary and sufficient representability conditions, or produce a minimal
   counterexample.

3. **Formalize CSS distance, not only graph girth.**  Introduce Hamming weight on
   finite binary cochains and define primal and dual logical distances as minima
   over nonzero homology and cohomology classes.  Prove the standard
   `min(systole, cosystole)` theorem under explicit finiteness and nondegeneracy
   assumptions.  This will prevent the primal girth from being mistaken for the
   complete quantum distance.

4. **Construct the actual hypercube incidence complex.**  The bridge theorem in
   `HypercubeCounterexample.lean` is parameterized by dimensions, connectedness,
   and a zero 2-boundary.  Define oriented edges and the boundary matrix over
   `ZMod 2`, prove its rank is `2^n-1`, and instantiate the theorem directly.

5. **Test other meanings of “hypercube complex.”**  The cube graph, the filled
   cubical `n`-ball, its boundary sphere, and periodic cubical tori have different
   homology.  Formalizing all four would isolate which object, if any, could have
   motivated a one-logical-qubit assertion.

6. **Add quantum-code bounds with the correct block length.**  Compare the proved
   parameters against the quantum Singleton bound using the number of physical
   edge qubits `N=n·2^(n-1)`, rather than using the cube dimension `n` as though it
   were block length.

-- NEW_FILE: Catalog/Geometry/CSSDictionary.lean
import Shared.HQECC.CSSHomology

/-!
# The CSS dictionary: parity-check matrices ⟷ chain complex ⟷ stabilizer group

This file carries out **future target 1** of the previous research cycle.  The
cycle proved the dimension formula for an abstract length-two chain complex
`A --d₂--> B --d₁--> C`, and *described* CSS codes by the informal expression
`C₁/C₂` with `C₂ ⊆ C₁`.  That description is incomplete in two ways: the usual
CSS commutation condition is `H_X H_Zᵀ = 0`, phrased with orthogonal
complements, and the object it produces is a *stabilizer group*, which never
appeared.  We give here the exact equivalence of the three pictures.

Throughout, a classical linear code is presented by a parity-check matrix.  For
`H : Matrix m N K` we write

* `code H  = ker (v ↦ H *ᵥ v)`      — the code it checks;
* `rowSpace H = range (y ↦ Hᵀ *ᵥ y)` — the code generated by its checks;
* `perp W` — the orthogonal complement for the standard bilinear form
  `⟪v, w⟫ = v ⬝ᵥ w` (which is nondegenerate: `perp_top`).

The three faces of the dictionary, for a pair `H_X, H_Z` of parity checks:

1. **Inclusion of classical codes** `rowSpace H_Z ≤ code H_X`, i.e. the mission's
   `C₂ ⊆ C₁` (`rowSpace_le_code_iff`);
2. **Orthogonality/commutation of parity checks** `H_X H_Zᵀ = 0`
   (`code_eq_perp_rowSpace` identifies `code H = perp (rowSpace H)`, so 1 is
   literally an orthogonality statement);
3. **Isotropy of the stabilizer group** for the symplectic (Pauli-commutation)
   form on `𝔽₂^N × 𝔽₂^N` (`stabilizer_isotropic_iff`): the group generated by
   the `X`-type checks and the `Z`-type checks is abelian.

`cssComplex` then packages such a pair as an honest `CSSComplex` whose cycles
are `C₁ = code H_X`, whose boundaries are `C₂ = rowSpace H_Z`, and whose
homology is therefore *the* quotient `C₁/C₂`; `cssComplex_numLogical_add`
recovers the CSS count `k = N − rank H_X − rank H_Z`, and
`cssComplex_numLogical_quotient` states it in the `C₁/C₂` form.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
HYPOTHESIS (Hypothesizer).  The three formulations (inclusion of classical
codes, matrix orthogonality, isotropy of the stabilizer) are *equivalent*, and
the equivalence is an identity of submodules rather than a numerical
coincidence.

EXPERIMENT (Experimenter).  `rowSpace_le_code_iff` is proved by the adjunction
`(Hᵀ *ᵥ y) ⬝ᵥ v = y ⬝ᵥ (H *ᵥ v)` plus nondegeneracy of the dot product;
isotropy is proved by a double `Submodule.span_le` argument through the flip of
the symplectic form, so no basis or finiteness of the generating set is used.

ANALYSIS (Analyst).  The `X/Z` symmetry of CSS codes is exactly the transpose
symmetry of `H_X H_Zᵀ = 0` (`commutation_symm`).  The count
`k + rank H_X + rank H_Z = N` needs `Matrix.rank_transpose` — the only place a
field is required; the inclusion/isotropy equivalences hold over any
commutative ring with a nondegenerate dot product.

CRITIQUE (Critic).  `perp` is only well behaved because the standard form is
nondegenerate; `perp_top` records this, and no result below silently assumes
`perp (perp W) = W`.  The isotropy theorem is an iff, so it cannot be satisfied
vacuously: its right-to-left direction genuinely evaluates the form on the
generators.
-/

namespace HQECC
namespace CSSDictionary

open Matrix Module

/-! ## Classical codes from parity-check matrices -/

variable {K : Type*} [Field K] {m mx mz N : Type*}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype mx] [Fintype mz] [Fintype N]

/-- The classical code checked by `H`: `C(H) = ker H`. -/
def code (H : Matrix m N K) : Submodule K (N → K) := LinearMap.ker H.mulVecLin

/-- The code *generated* by the rows of `H`, i.e. the row space `im Hᵀ`. -/
def rowSpace (H : Matrix m N K) : Submodule K (N → K) := LinearMap.range Hᵀ.mulVecLin

omit [Fintype m] in
@[simp] lemma mem_code {H : Matrix m N K} {v : N → K} : v ∈ code H ↔ H *ᵥ v = 0 :=
  Iff.rfl

omit [Fintype N] in
lemma mem_rowSpace {H : Matrix m N K} {w : N → K} :
    w ∈ rowSpace H ↔ ∃ y : m → K, Hᵀ *ᵥ y = w := Iff.rfl

/-- The orthogonal complement of a subspace of `Kᴺ` for the standard bilinear
form `⟪v, w⟫ = v ⬝ᵥ w`. -/
def perp (W : Submodule K (N → K)) : Submodule K (N → K) where
  carrier := {v | ∀ w ∈ W, w ⬝ᵥ v = 0}
  zero_mem' := by intro w _; simp
  add_mem' := by
    intro a b ha hb w hw
    rw [dotProduct_add, ha w hw, hb w hw, add_zero]
  smul_mem' := by
    intro c a ha w hw
    rw [dotProduct_smul, ha w hw, smul_zero]

lemma mem_perp {W : Submodule K (N → K)} {v : N → K} :
    v ∈ perp W ↔ ∀ w ∈ W, w ⬝ᵥ v = 0 := Iff.rfl

/-- **Nondegeneracy** of the standard form: only `0` is orthogonal to
everything. -/
theorem perp_top : perp (⊤ : Submodule K (N → K)) = ⊥ := by
  ext v
  simp only [mem_perp, Submodule.mem_bot]
  constructor
  · intro h
    have hall : ∀ w : N → K, v ⬝ᵥ w = 0 := by

# The CSS dictionary: parity-check matrices ⟷ chain complex ⟷ stabilizer group

This file carries out **future target 1** of the previous research cycle.  The
cycle proved the dimension formula for an abstract length-two chain complex
`A --d₂--> B --d₁--> C`, and *described* CSS codes by the informal expression
`C₁/C₂` with `C₂ ⊆ C₁`.  That description is incomplete in two ways: the usual
CSS commutation condition is `H_X H_Zᵀ = 0`, phrased with orthogonal
complements, and the object it produces is a *stabilizer group*, which never
appeared.  We give here the exact equivalence of the three pictures.

Throughout, a classical linear code is presented by a parity-check matrix.  For
`H : Matrix m N K` we write

* `code H  = ker (v ↦ H *ᵥ v)`      — the code it checks;
* `rowSpace H = range (y ↦ Hᵀ *ᵥ y)` — the code generated by its checks;
* `perp W` — the orthogonal complement for the standard bilinear form
  `⟪v, w⟫ = v ⬝ᵥ w` (which is nondegenerate: `perp_top`).

The three faces of the dictionary, for a pair `H_X, H_Z` of parity checks:

1. **Inclusion of classical codes** `rowSpace H_Z ≤ code H_X`, i.e. the mission's
   `C₂ ⊆ C₁` (`rowSpace_le_code_iff`);
2. **Orthogonality/commutation of parity checks** `H_X H_Zᵀ = 0`
   (`code_eq_perp_rowSpace` identifies `code H = perp (rowSpace H)`, so 1 is
   literally an orthogonality statement);

   the `X`-type checks and the `Z`-type checks is abelian.

are `C₁ = code H_X`, whose boundaries are `C₂ = rowSpace H_Z`, and whose
homology is therefore *the* quotient `C₁/C₂`; `cssComplex_numLogical_add`

`cssComplex_numLogical_quotient` states it in the `C₁/C₂` form.

HYPOTHESIS (Hypothesizer).  The three formulations (inclusion of classical
codes, matrix orthogonality, isotropy of the stabilizer) are *equivalent*, and
the equivalence is an identity of submodules rather than a numerical

    (by intro c p q; simp [smul_dotProduct, dotProduct_smul, smul_eq_mul]; ring)

def stabGens (Hx : Matrix mx N (ZMod 2)) (Hz : Matrix mz N (ZMod 2)) :

    Set.range (fun j : mz => ((0 : N → ZMod 2), Hz j))

  ⟨rowSpace_le_code_iff Hx Hz, (stabilizer_isotropic_iff Hx Hz).symm⟩

end Stabilizer

end CSSDictionary
end HQECC

/-!
# CSS distance: Hamming weight, logical operators, and `min(systole, cosystole)`

This file carries out **future target 3** of the research thread.  The previous
cycle computed the *girth* of the hypercube graph and warned that girth is not
the quantum distance; but no notion of CSS distance existed in the catalog, so
the warning could not be made precise.  Here we define it.

For a commuting pair of binary parity-check matrices `H_X, H_Z` on `N` physical
qubits (see `Catalog/Geometry/CSSDictionary.lean`):

* `wt a` — Hamming weight of a binary cochain, `wtPair p` — weight of a Pauli
  operator `p = (a, b)` (the size of the union of the two supports);
* `XLogical`/`ZLogical` — the *nontrivial undetectable* single-type errors, i.e.
  representatives of nonzero homology (resp. cohomology) classes;
* `dX`/`dZ` — the primal and dual logical distances (systole and cosystole);
* `Undetectable` — errors commuting with every stabilizer, and `cssDistance` —
  the minimum weight of an undetectable error outside the stabilizer group.

The main theorem `cssDistance_eq_min` is the standard
`d = min(systole, cosystole)` statement, proved under explicit nondegeneracy
hypotheses (`hX`, `hZ`: both logical sets are nonempty, i.e. the code really has
`X`- and `Z`-logicals).  Its proof needs the structural lemma
`stab_eq_prod`: the stabilizer group is the *product* `rowSpace H_X × rowSpace H_Z`
of the two trivial-operator subspaces.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
HYPOTHESIS (Hypothesizer).  A general undetectable Pauli error mixes `X` and `Z`
parts, so a priori the code distance could be *strictly smaller* than both
single-type distances.  We conjecture it cannot: the weight of a mixed error
dominates the weight of each of its parts, and nontriviality of the pair forces
nontriviality of at least one part.

EXPERIMENT (Experimenter).  Formalised with `Nat.sInf` over weight sets.  The
key step is `stab_eq_prod`, proved by writing `Hᵀ *ᵥ y` as the row combination
`∑ i, y i • H i` and using `Submodule.sum_mem` in both directions.

ANALYSIS (Analyst).  The two nondegeneracy hypotheses are genuinely needed:
`Nat.sInf ∅ = 0`, so without them the theorem would silently degenerate.  With
them the infimum is attained (`Nat.sInf_mem`), which is what makes the `≥`
direction work.

CRITIQUE (Critic).  `cssDistance` is defined by an operational condition
("undetectable but not a stabilizer"), *not* as `min dX dZ`; the theorem is
therefore not definitional.  A mixed error is allowed in the competition, and
the proof must genuinely rule out that it beats both single-type distances.

namespace HQECC
namespace CSSDistance

open Matrix Module CSSDictionary

variable {mx mz N : Type*} [Fintype mx] [Fintype mz] [Fintype N] [DecidableEq N]

/-! ## Hamming weight -/

/-- The Hamming weight of a binary cochain. -/
def wt (a : N → ZMod 2) : ℕ := (Finset.univ.filter (fun i => a i ≠ 0)).card

/-- The weight of a phase-free Pauli operator `p = (a, b)`: the number of
qubits on which it acts nontrivially. -/
def wtPair (p : (N → ZMod 2) × (N → ZMod 2)) : ℕ :=
  ((Finset.univ.filter (fun i => p.1 i ≠ 0)) ∪
    (Finset.univ.filter (fun i => p.2 i ≠ 0))).card

lemma wt_le_wtPair_left (p : (N → ZMod 2) × (N → ZMod 2)) : wt p.1 ≤ wtPair p :=
  Finset.card_le_card Finset.subset_union_left

lemma wt_le_wtPair_right (p : (N → ZMod 2) × (N → ZMod 2)) : wt p.2 ≤ wtPair p :=
  Finset.card_le_card Finset.subset_union_right

@[simp] lemma wtPair_left (a : N → ZMod 2) : wtPair (a, 0) = wt a := by
  simp [wtPair, wt]

@[simp] lemma wtPair_right (b : N → ZMod 2) : wtPair (0, b) = wt b := by
  simp [wtPair, wt]

omit [DecidableEq N] in
lemma wt_eq_zero_iff {a : N → ZMod 2} : wt a = 0 ↔ a = 0 := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    have hempty := Finset.card_eq_zero.1 h
    ext i
    by_contra hi
    have : i ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun i => a i ≠ 0) :=
      Finset.mem_filter.2 ⟨Finset.mem_univ i, by simpa using hi⟩
    rw [hempty] at this
    exact absurd this (Finset.notMem_empty i)
  · rintro rfl; simp [wt]

lemma wtPair_pos {p : (N → ZMod 2) × (N → ZMod 2)} (hp : p ≠ 0) : 0 < wtPair p := by
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (wtPair p) with h | h
  · exfalso
    have h1 : wt p.1 = 0 := Nat.le_zero.1 (h ▸ wt_le_wtPair_left p)
    have h2 : wt p.2 = 0 := Nat.le_zero.1 (h ▸ wt_le_wtPair_right p)
    exact hp (Prod.ext (wt_eq_zero_iff.1 h1) (wt_eq_zero_iff.1 h2))
  · exact h

/-! ## Logical operators -/

variable (Hx : Matrix mx N (ZMod 2)) (Hz : Matrix mz N (ZMod 2))

/-- A nontrivial undetectable `X`-type error: it commutes with all `Z`-checks
(`H_Z a = 0`) but is not a product of `X`-stabilizers. -/
def XLogical (a : N → ZMod 2) : Prop := Hz *ᵥ a = 0 ∧ a ∉ rowSpace Hx

/-- A nontrivial undetectable `Z`-type error. -/
def ZLogical (b : N → ZMod 2) : Prop := Hx *ᵥ b = 0 ∧ b ∉ rowSpace Hz

/-- The **primal distance** (systole): least weight of a nontrivial
undetectable `X`-error. -/
noncomputable def dX : ℕ := sInf {w | ∃ a, XLogical Hx Hz a ∧ wt a = w}

/-- The **dual distance** (cosystole): least weight of a nontrivial
undetectable `Z`-error. -/
noncomputable def dZ : ℕ := sInf {w | ∃ b, ZLogical Hx Hz b ∧ wt b = w}

/-- A Pauli error is **undetectable** when it commutes with every stabilizer
generator: its `X`-part passes the `Z`-checks and its `Z`-part the `X`-checks. -/
def Undetectable (p : (N → ZMod 2) × (N → ZMod 2)) : Prop :=
  Hz *ᵥ p.1 = 0 ∧ Hx *ᵥ p.2 = 0

/-- The **CSS distance**: least weight of an undetectable error that is not a
stabilizer.  This is the operational quantity; it is *not* defined as a minimum
of the two single-type distances. -/
noncomputable def cssDistance : ℕ :=
  sInf {w | ∃ p, Undetectable Hx Hz p ∧ p ∉ stab Hx Hz ∧ wtPair p = w}

/-! ## The stabilizer group is a product of row spaces -/

omit [Fintype N] [DecidableEq N] in
/-- `Hᵀ *ᵥ y` is the row combination `∑ i, y i • H i`. -/
lemma transpose_mulVec_eq_sum (H : Matrix mx N (ZMod 2)) (y : mx → ZMod 2) :
    Hᵀ *ᵥ y = ∑ i, y i • H i := by
  funext j
  simp [Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, Finset.sum_apply, mul_comm]

omit [Fintype N] [DecidableEq N] in
/-- **The stabilizer group is `rowSpace H_X × rowSpace H_Z`.**  Consequently an
error `(a, b)` is a *nontrivial* logical operator exactly when `a` fails to be a
product of `X`-stabilizers or `b` fails to be a product of `Z`-stabilizers. -/
theorem stab_eq_prod :
    stab Hx Hz = (rowSpace Hx).prod (rowSpace Hz) := by
  classical
  apply le_antisymm
  · rw [stab, Submodule.span_le]
    rintro p (⟨i, rfl⟩ | ⟨j, rfl⟩)
    · refine ⟨?_, Submodule.zero_mem _⟩
      refine ⟨Pi.single i 1, ?_⟩
      rw [Matrix.mulVecLin_apply, transpose_mulVec_eq_sum]
      simp [Pi.single_apply, Finset.sum_ite_eq']
    · refine ⟨Submodule.zero_mem _, ?_⟩
      refine ⟨Pi.single j 1, ?_⟩
      rw [Matrix.mulVecLin_apply, transpose_mulVec_eq_sum]
      simp [Pi.single_apply, Finset.sum_ite_eq']
  · rintro ⟨a, b⟩ ⟨⟨y, hy⟩, ⟨z, hz⟩⟩
    have ha : ((a, (0 : N → ZMod 2)) : (N → ZMod 2) × (N → ZMod 2)) ∈ stab Hx Hz := by
      rw [Matrix.mulVecLin_apply, transpose_mulVec_eq_sum] at hy
      subst hy
      have : ((∑ i, y i • Hx i, (0 : N → ZMod 2)) : (N → ZMod 2) × (N → ZMod 2)) =
          ∑ i, y i • ((Hx i, (0 : N → ZMod 2)) : (N → ZMod 2) × (N → ZMod 2)) := by
        simp [Prod.ext_iff, Prod.fst_sum, Prod.snd_sum]
      rw [this]
      exact Submodule.sum_mem _ (fun i _ =>
        Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (Submodule.subset_span (Or.inl ⟨i, rfl⟩)))
    have hb : (((0 : N → ZMod 2), b) : (N → ZMod 2) × (N → ZMod 2)) ∈ stab Hx Hz := by
      rw [Matrix.mulVecLin_apply, transpose_mulVec_eq_sum] at hz
      subst hz
      have : (((0 : N → ZMod 2), ∑ j, z j • Hz j) : (N → ZMod 2) × (N → ZMod 2)) =
          ∑ j, z j • (((0 : N → ZMod 2), Hz j) : (N → ZMod 2) × (N → ZMod 2)) := by
        simp [Prod.ext_iff, Prod.fst_sum, Prod.snd_sum]
      rw [this]
      exact Submodule.sum_mem _ (fun j _ =>
        Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (Submodule.subset_span (Or.inr ⟨j, rfl⟩)))
    have := Submodule.add_mem _ ha hb
    simpa using this

omit [Fintype N] [DecidableEq N] in
/-- Membership in the stabilizer group is componentwise. -/
lemma mem_stab_iff {p : (N → ZMod 2) × (N → ZMod 2)} :
    p ∈ stab Hx Hz ↔ p.1 ∈ rowSpace Hx ∧ p.2 ∈ rowSpace Hz := by
  rw [stab_eq_prod]
  exact Submodule.mem_prod

/-! ## `d = min(systole, cosystole)` -/

/-- A minimal-weight `X`-logical, paired with the identity `Z`-part, is an
undetectable nonstabilizer error of weight `dX`. -/
lemma cssDistance_le_dX (hX : {w | ∃ a, XLogical Hx Hz a ∧ wt a = w}.Nonempty) :
    cssDistance Hx Hz ≤ dX Hx Hz := by
  obtain ⟨a, ha, hwa⟩ := Nat.sInf_mem hX
  refine Nat.sInf_le ⟨(a, 0), ⟨ha.1, by simp⟩, ?_, by simpa using hwa⟩
  rw [mem_stab_iff]
  rintro ⟨h1, -⟩
  exact ha.2 h1

/-- Dual version of `cssDistance_le_dX`. -/
lemma cssDistance_le_dZ (hZ : {w | ∃ b, ZLogical Hx Hz b ∧ wt b = w}.Nonempty) :
    cssDistance Hx Hz ≤ dZ Hx Hz := by
  obtain ⟨b, hb, hwb⟩ := Nat.sInf_mem hZ
  refine Nat.sInf_le ⟨(0, b), ⟨by simp, hb.1⟩, ?_, by simpa using hwb⟩
  rw [mem_stab_iff]
  rintro ⟨-, h2⟩
  exact hb.2 h2

/-- **The CSS distance theorem.**  Under the nondegeneracy hypotheses that both
kinds of logical operator exist, the operational distance of the code equals
`min(systole, cosystole)`.  In particular the primal quantity alone (for a graph
code: the girth) is *not* the distance. -/
theorem cssDistance_eq_min
    (hX : {w | ∃ a, XLogical Hx Hz a ∧ wt a = w}.Nonempty)
    (hZ : {w | ∃ b, ZLogical Hx Hz b ∧ wt b = w}.Nonempty) :
    cssDistance Hx Hz = min (dX Hx Hz) (dZ Hx Hz) := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · exact le_min (cssDistance_le_dX Hx Hz hX) (cssDistance_le_dZ Hx Hz hZ)
  · have hne : {w | ∃ p, Undetectable Hx Hz p ∧ p ∉ stab Hx Hz ∧ wtPair p = w}.Nonempty := by
      obtain ⟨a, ha, hwa⟩ := Nat.sInf_mem hX
      refine ⟨wt a, (a, 0), ⟨ha.1, by simp⟩, ?_, by simp⟩
      rw [mem_stab_iff]
      rintro ⟨h1, -⟩
      exact ha.2 h1
    obtain ⟨p, hund, hstab, hwp⟩ := Nat.sInf_mem hne
    rw [mem_stab_iff] at hstab
    rw [not_and_or] at hstab
    rcases hstab with h1 | h2
    · have hXlog : XLogical Hx Hz p.1 := ⟨hund.1, h1⟩
      have : dX Hx Hz ≤ wt p.1 := Nat.sInf_le ⟨p.1, hXlog, rfl⟩
      calc min (dX Hx Hz) (dZ Hx Hz) ≤ dX Hx Hz := min_le_left _ _
        _ ≤ wt p.1 := this
        _ ≤ wtPair p := wt_le_wtPair_left p
        _ = cssDistance Hx Hz := hwp
    · have hZlog : ZLogical Hx Hz p.2 := ⟨hund.2, h2⟩
      have : dZ Hx Hz ≤ wt p.2 := Nat.sInf_le ⟨p.2, hZlog, rfl⟩
      calc min (dX Hx Hz) (dZ Hx Hz) ≤ dZ Hx Hz := min_le_right _ _
        _ ≤ wt p.2 := this
        _ ≤ wtPair p := wt_le_wtPair_right p
        _ = cssDistance Hx Hz := hwp

omit [Fintype mx] [Fintype mz] in
/-- The distance is at least `1` whenever some undetectable nonstabilizer error
exists: a weight-`0` error is the identity, which is a stabilizer. -/
theorem one_le_cssDistance
    (hne : {w | ∃ p, Undetectable Hx Hz p ∧ p ∉ stab Hx Hz ∧ wtPair p = w}.Nonempty) :
    1 ≤ cssDistance Hx Hz := by
  obtain ⟨p, -, hstab, hwp⟩ := Nat.sInf_mem hne
  have hp : p ≠ 0 := by
    rintro rfl
    exact hstab (Submodule.zero_mem _)
  exact le_of_le_of_eq (wtPair_pos hp) hwp

end CSSDistance
end HQECC

import Geometry.SteaneCode
import Geometry.HypercubeIncidence

/-!
# Which binary CSS complexes come from a graph?  A rank obstruction

This file carries out **future target 2** of the research thread: *separate the
graph/simplicial model from the abstract chain-complex model*.  The previous
cycle proved a dimension theorem for arbitrary differentials over a field and
then applied it to a graph; the implicit assumption that every binary CSS
complex is realised by an incidence matrix of an actual `1`-complex is a
strictly stronger claim.  We refute it, with a clean necessary condition.

A `𝔽₂` matrix is a **graph incidence matrix** when every column is the indicator
of a pair of distinct vertices (`IsGraphIncidence`).  The key observation is a
*parity obstruction*: every such column has weight `2`, so the all-ones row
vector annihilates the matrix.  Hence

  `rank M + 1 ≤ #V`   (`IsGraphIncidence.rank_lt`),

i.e. the `X`-checks of a graph code are **never** independent.  Consequently any
CSS code whose `X`-check matrix has full row rank — for instance the Steane code
(`steaneH_not_graph_incidence`) — cannot be realised by a graph with its
standard incidence maps, however one chooses the vertex set.  The smallest
counterexample is the `1 × 1` matrix `[1]` (`one_by_one_not_graph_incidence`).

Conversely the hypercube boundary matrix built in
`Catalog/Geometry/HypercubeIncidence.lean` *is* a graph incidence matrix
(`incid_isGraphIncidence`), so the obstruction is not vacuous, and its
corank-one behaviour (`rank_incid_add_one`) is an instance of the general bound
above — an equality, since `Qₙ` is connected.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
HYPOTHESIS (Hypothesizer).  Representability by a `1`-complex is not automatic;
we conjecture a *linear-algebraic* obstruction visible already at the level of
ranks, not just a combinatorial one.

EXPERIMENT (Experimenter).  Every column of a graph incidence matrix has exactly
two `1`s, so its entries sum to `0` in `𝔽₂`: the all-ones vector lies in
`ker Mᵀ`, which forces `rank M < #V`.  Applied to `steaneH` (rank `3` on `3`
rows) this gives an immediate contradiction.

ANALYSIS (Analyst).  The condition is necessary but not sufficient: it says
nothing about the `Z`-side or about weights.  A full characterisation would have
to control the column weights (`2` for graphs, `k+1` for simplicial `k`-cells),
which is exactly the point of separating the models.

CRITIQUE (Critic).  `IsGraphIncidence` demands the two endpoints be *distinct*,
ruling out the degenerate "loop" columns; without that the obstruction fails,
since a loop column is `0`.  The counterexample is therefore stated with the
honest definition.
-/

namespace HQECC
namespace GraphRepresentability

open Matrix Module CSSDictionary

variable {V E : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Fintype E]

/-- `M` is the incidence matrix of a graph: every column is the indicator of a
pair of *distinct* vertices — the two endpoints of the corresponding edge. -/
def IsGraphIncidence (M : Matrix V E (ZMod 2)) : Prop :=
  ∀ e : E, ∃ u v : V, u ≠ v ∧
    ∀ w, M w e = (if w = u then 1 else 0) + (if w = v then 1 else 0)

omit [Fintype E] in
/-- **Parity obstruction.**  Each column of a graph incidence matrix has weight
`2`, hence sums to `0` over `𝔽₂`. -/
theorem IsGraphIncidence.column_sum {M : Matrix V E (ZMod 2)} (hM : IsGraphIncidence M)
    (e : E) : ∑ w, M w e = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨u, v, -, hcol⟩ := hM e
  simp only [hcol, Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_ite_eq', Finset.mem_univ, if_true]
  decide

omit [Fintype E] in
/-- The all-ones vector is a cocycle of a graph incidence matrix. -/
theorem IsGraphIncidence.one_mem_ker {M : Matrix V E (ZMod 2)} (hM : IsGraphIncidence M) :
    (1 : V → ZMod 2) ∈ LinearMap.ker (Mᵀ.mulVecLin) := by
  ext e
  rw [Matrix.mulVecLin_apply]
  simpa [Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, Matrix.transpose_apply] using hM.column_sum e

/-- **The checks of a graph code are never independent**: `rank M < #V`.
(The vertex set is nonempty because `V` carries the all-ones vector `≠ 0`.) -/
theorem IsGraphIncidence.rank_lt [Nonempty V] {M : Matrix V E (ZMod 2)}
    (hM : IsGraphIncidence M) : M.rank + 1 ≤ Fintype.card V := by
  have hone : (1 : V → ZMod 2) ≠ 0 := by
    intro h
    have := congrFun h (Classical.arbitrary V)
    simp at this
  have hker : 1 ≤ finrank (ZMod 2) (LinearMap.ker (Mᵀ.mulVecLin)) := by
    have hsub : Submodule.span (ZMod 2) {(1 : V → ZMod 2)} ≤ LinearMap.ker (Mᵀ.mulVecLin) := by
      rw [Submodule.span_le]
      rintro g rfl
      exact hM.one_mem_ker
    have h1 : finrank (ZMod 2) (Submodule.span (ZMod 2) {(1 : V → ZMod 2)}) = 1 :=
      finrank_span_singleton hone
    have := Submodule.finrank_mono hsub
    omega
  have hrn := LinearMap.finrank_range_add_finrank_ker (Mᵀ.mulVecLin)
  rw [Module.finrank_fintype_fun_eq_card] at hrn
  have hT : Mᵀ.rank = M.rank := Matrix.rank_transpose _
  have hrange : finrank (ZMod 2) (LinearMap.range (Mᵀ.mulVecLin)) = M.rank := hT
  omega

/-! ## The hypercube boundary matrix is a graph incidence matrix -/

open HypercubeIncidence in
/-- The hypercube boundary matrix of `HypercubeIncidence.lean` really is the
incidence matrix of a graph. -/
theorem incid_isGraphIncidence (n : ℕ) : IsGraphIncidence (incid n) := by
  intro e
  refine ⟨(e.2 : Vert n), (e.2 : Vert n) + bit e.1, ?_, fun w => rfl⟩
  intro h
  have h1 : ((e.2 : Vert n) + bit e.1) e.1 = (e.2 : Vert n) e.1 := by rw [← h]
  rw [Pi.add_apply, e.2.2] at h1
  simp [bit] at h1

/-! ## Counterexamples: CSS complexes with no graph model -/

/-- **The Steane code is not a graph code.**  Its `X`-check matrix has full row
rank `3`, contradicting `rank < #V` for any graph model on `3` vertices. -/
theorem steaneH_not_graph_incidence : ¬ IsGraphIncidence SteaneCode.steaneH := by
  intro h
  have := h.rank_lt
  rw [SteaneCode.steaneH_rank] at this
  simp at this

/-- **The minimal counterexample.**  The `1 × 1` matrix `[1]` is a perfectly
good binary differential (`d₁ = id`, `d₂ = 0` is a chain complex) but is not the
incidence matrix of any graph: a single column cannot be the indicator of two
distinct vertices among one vertex. -/
theorem one_by_one_not_graph_incidence :
    ¬ IsGraphIncidence (1 : Matrix (Fin 1) (Fin 1) (ZMod 2)) := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨u, v, huv, -⟩ := h 0
  exact huv (Subsingleton.elim u v)

end GraphRepresentability
end HQECC

import Geometry.CSSDistance
import Geometry.HypercubeIncidence

/-!
# The hypercube homological code has CSS distance `1`

The previous research cycle proved that the hypercube graph `Qₙ` has girth `4`
for every `n ≥ 2` and warned that the girth "should not be mistaken for the
complete quantum distance".  With the CSS distance now defined
(`Catalog/Geometry/CSSDistance.lean`) we can settle the question quantitatively.

The homological code `HQECC(Qₙ)` is the CSS code with
`H_X = ∂₁` (one `X`-check per vertex) and **no** `Z`-checks: a graph carries no
`2`-cells.  Its dual distance is the girth `4` (the lightest nonzero cycle), but
its *primal* distance is the lightest edge set that is **not** a cut, and a
single edge of `Qₙ` is not a cut, because it lies on a square.  Hence

  `dX = 1`   and therefore   `d = min(dX, dZ) = 1`.

So `HQECC(Qₙ)` corrects **no** errors: the parameters are `[[n·2ⁿ⁻¹,
2ⁿ⁻¹(n−2)+1, 1]]`, not `[[·, 1, 2^{n/2}]]`, and the girth `4` measures only one
of the two logical sectors.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
HYPOTHESIS (Hypothesizer).  A graph code has trivial `Z`-stabilizer group, so
*every* edge subset is an undetectable `X`-error; its `X`-distance is the
minimal weight of a non-cut, which is `1` unless the graph has a bridge.  We
conjecture `dX(Qₙ) = 1` for all `n ≥ 2`, i.e. the true distance is `1`.

EXPERIMENT (Experimenter).  The witness is the indicator of a single edge.  The
proof that it is not a coboundary is a four-term telescoping identity around a
square of the cube: summing the coboundary condition over the four edges of the
square makes every vertex value appear twice, giving `0 = 1` in `𝔽₂`.

ANALYSIS (Analyst).  This isolates the error in the "systolic scaling" picture:
the systole of a *graph* controls only `dZ`.  Obtaining a growing CSS distance
requires genuine `2`-cells (as in the toric code), not just a high-girth graph.

CRITIQUE (Critic).  The result is a strict strengthening, not a restatement, of
the previous cycle's girth computation: it produces an explicit weight-one
undetectable nonstabilizer error, and `one_le_cssDistance` rules out the
degenerate value `0` coming from `Nat.sInf ∅ = 0`.
-/

namespace HQECC
namespace HypercubeDistanceOne

open Matrix CSSDictionary CSSDistance HypercubeIncidence

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- The `Z`-check matrix of a graph code: there are no `2`-cells, hence no
`Z`-checks. -/
def noZChecks (n : ℕ) : Matrix (Fin 0) (Edge n) (ZMod 2) := 0

/-- Two distinct directions of the cube, available as soon as `n ≥ 2`. -/
lemma exists_two_directions (hn : 2 ≤ n) : ∃ i0 i1 : Fin n, i0 ≠ i1 :=
  ⟨⟨0, by omega⟩, ⟨1, by omega⟩, by simp [Fin.ext_iff]⟩

/-- **A single edge is not a cut.**  For `n ≥ 2` the indicator function of the
edge `⟨i0, 0⟩` is not in the row space of the incidence matrix, i.e. it is not a
coboundary.  The proof adds the coboundary equation over the four edges of the
square spanned by the directions `i0 ≠ i1`. -/
theorem single_edge_not_coboundary (i0 i1 : Fin n) (h01 : i0 ≠ i1) :
    (Pi.single (⟨i0, ⟨0, rfl⟩⟩ : Edge n) 1 : Edge n → ZMod 2) ∉ rowSpace (incid n) := by
  rintro ⟨f, hf⟩
  rw [Matrix.mulVecLin_apply] at hf
  have h10 : i1 ≠ i0 := fun h => h01 h.symm
  have hb1i0 : (bit i1) i0 = 0 := by simp [bit, h01]
  have hb0i1 : (bit i0) i1 = 0 := by simp [bit, h10]
  -- the coboundary equation, at an arbitrary edge
  have key : ∀ e : Edge n, f (e.2 : Vert n) + f ((e.2 : Vert n) + bit e.1) =
      (Pi.single (⟨i0, ⟨0, rfl⟩⟩ : Edge n) 1 : Edge n → ZMod 2) e := by
    intro e
    rw [← incid_transpose_mulVec n f e, hf]
  -- the four edges of the square through `0` spanned by the directions `i0`, `i1`
  have k0 := key ⟨i0, ⟨0, rfl⟩⟩
  have ka := key ⟨i0, ⟨bit i1, hb1i0⟩⟩
  have kb := key ⟨i1, ⟨0, rfl⟩⟩
  have kc := key ⟨i1, ⟨bit i0, hb0i1⟩⟩
  simp only [zero_add] at k0 ka kb kc
  rw [Pi.single_eq_same] at k0
  rw [Pi.single_eq_of_ne (by
    intro h
    have hh : (bit i1 : Vert n) = 0 := congrArg (fun e : Edge n => (e.2 : Vert n)) h
    have h1 : (bit i1 : Vert n) i1 = 1 := by simp [bit]
    rw [hh] at h1
    exact absurd h1 (by simp)) 1] at ka
  rw [Pi.single_eq_of_ne (by intro h; exact h10 (congrArg Sigma.fst h)) 1] at kb
  rw [Pi.single_eq_of_ne (by intro h; exact h10 (congrArg Sigma.fst h)) 1] at kc
  rw [add_comm (bit i1) (bit i0)] at ka
  -- summing the four equations: every vertex value occurs twice, so `1 = 0`
  have square : ∀ p q r s : ZMod 2, (p + q) + ((r + s) + ((p + r) + (q + s))) = 0 := by decide
  have hcontra := square (f 0) (f (bit i0)) (f (bit i1)) (f (bit i0 + bit i1))
  rw [k0, ka, kb, kc] at hcontra
  exact absurd hcontra (by decide)

/-- The single-edge indicator has Hamming weight `1`. -/
lemma wt_single (e : Edge n) : wt (Pi.single e 1 : Edge n → ZMod 2) = 1 := by
  unfold wt
  rw [show (Finset.univ.filter (fun x => (Pi.single e 1 : Edge n → ZMod 2) x ≠ 0)) = {e} by
    ext x
    simp [Pi.single_apply, eq_comm]]
  simp

/-- **The primal distance of the hypercube graph code is `1`.** -/
theorem hypercube_dX_eq_one (hn : 2 ≤ n) : dX (incid n) (noZChecks n) = 1 := by
  obtain ⟨i0, i1, h01⟩ := exists_two_directions hn
  have hmem : (1 : ℕ) ∈ {w | ∃ a, XLogical (incid n) (noZChecks n) a ∧ wt a = w} := by
    refine ⟨Pi.single (⟨i0, ⟨0, rfl⟩⟩ : Edge n) 1, ⟨?_, single_edge_not_coboundary i0 i1 h01⟩,
      wt_single _⟩
    ext i
    exact absurd i.isLt (by omega)
  refine le_antisymm (Nat.sInf_le hmem) ?_
  by_contra hlt
  push_neg at hlt
  interval_cases h : dX (incid n) (noZChecks n)
  · obtain ⟨a, ha, hwa⟩ := Nat.sInf_mem (⟨1, hmem⟩ : Set.Nonempty _)
    rw [dX] at h
    rw [h] at hwa
    rw [wt_eq_zero_iff] at hwa
    subst hwa
    exact ha.2 (Submodule.zero_mem _)

/-- **The CSS distance of the hypercube homological code is `1`** for every
`n ≥ 2`: the code detects no error, in stark contrast with the girth `4` (which
bounds only the dual sector) and with the proposed value `2^{n/2}`. -/
theorem hypercube_cssDistance_eq_one (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    cssDistance (incid n) (noZChecks n) = 1 := by
  obtain ⟨i0, i1, h01⟩ := exists_two_directions hn
  set a : Edge n → ZMod 2 := Pi.single (⟨i0, ⟨0, rfl⟩⟩ : Edge n) 1 with ha
  have hnoZ : noZChecks n *ᵥ a = 0 := by
    ext i
    exact absurd i.isLt (by omega)
  have hns : ((a, 0) : (Edge n → ZMod 2) × (Edge n → ZMod 2)) ∉ stab (incid n) (noZChecks n) := by
    rw [mem_stab_iff]
    rintro ⟨h1, -⟩
    exact single_edge_not_coboundary i0 i1 h01 h1
  have hmem : (1 : ℕ) ∈
      {w | ∃ p, Undetectable (incid n) (noZChecks n) p ∧ p ∉ stab (incid n) (noZChecks n) ∧
        wtPair p = w} := by
    refine ⟨(a, 0), ⟨hnoZ, by simp⟩, hns, ?_⟩
    rw [wtPair_left, ha, wt_single]
  refine le_antisymm (Nat.sInf_le hmem) (one_le_cssDistance _ _ ⟨1, hmem⟩)

end HypercubeDistanceOne
